title: Analysis: Detection flow and refactoring proposal for stage fallthrough
body: Task/Issue URL: N/A — proactive analysis ## Description: Adds a comprehensive analysis document (`docs/detection-flow-analysis.md`) that maps the full detection pipeline in `lib/web.ts` and proposes a refactoring to fix a cross-stage blocking problem. ### What's in the document 1. **Complete flowchart** of the detection cascade: `_start()` → `findCmp()` → `detectPopups()` → `handlePopup()`, covering all four rule priority levels (site-specific, generic, heuristic, cosmetic). 2. **Definitive analysis** of the blocking problem: when a CMP's `detectCmp()` returns true in an earlier priority stage but `detectPopup()` returns false, all lower-priority stages are skipped entirely. Confirmed to affect 5 specific flows. 3. **Refactoring proposal** — "Concurrent Detection with Priority Gates": runs all stages' popup detection **concurrently** for maximum speed, but resolves results through a **priority-gated drain** so higher-priority stages always get preference. Includes: - **Speed asymmetry analysis**: heuristic rules resolve in ~50ms (synchronous DOM scan) vs. declarative rules taking up to ~5s (`waitForPopup` retries). A naive fallthrough would let heuristic pre-empt rules that just need more time. - **Grace period mechanism**: configurable delay (default 1500ms) before accepting heuristic results, giving higher-priority CMP scripts time to inject DOM elements. - **Detailed timeline walkthroughs** showing how the priority drain and grace period interact across key scenarios. - **New helper methods**: `detectPopupsForStage()`, `waitForPopupsSettled()`, `categorizeRules()` — separating popup detection from handling for priority resolution. - Performance analysis, behavioral change matrix, and migration risk assessment. ### Key findings - The cross-stage blocking hypothesis is **confirmed**: early-exit in `findCmp()` means a detected-but-popup-less CMP blocks all lower-priority rules. - The **priority drain** (awaiting stages in order) naturally provides the correct blocking: generic's ~5s of popup retries automatically delays the heuristic check. - The **grace period** addresses the edge case where no higher-priority CMP is detected at all but might appear on a subsequent retry. ## Steps to test this PR: This is a documentation-only PR. Review the analysis for accuracy against the current codebase: 1. Read the flowchart against `lib/web.ts` `_start()`, `findCmp()`, `detectPopups()`, and `waitForPopup()` 2. Verify the blocking scenarios described match the code behavior 3. Evaluate the concurrent detection + priority gate approach, particularly the grace period value for heuristic 4. Review the timeline walkthroughs in the "Why the priority drain works" section

title: osano: click close button on bar-type (permissive) popups
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215221044500981?focus=true ## Description: When Osano runs in permissive (CCPA) mode it shows a bar-type informational dialog whose only control is an `X` close button — no accept/deny choice. The optOut rule's `else` branch previously fell through to a CSS `hide`, which dismisses the popup visually but never updates Osano's internal state, so the consent is not persisted. This change clicks `.osano-cm-dialog__close` instead when the bar-type dialog is visible, letting Osano apply its own `--hidden` class and clear `dialogOpen`. The selector is gated on `.osano-cm-dialog--type_bar` so we don't risk clicking close on GDPR-style modal dialogs (box/full), where dismissing without a real reject button could be ambiguous. `hide` remains as the final fallback. `wearpact.com` is added to the osano test spec to cover this flavor. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. `npm run build-rules && npm run rule-syntax-check` 2. `npx playwright test tests/osano.spec.ts --project chrome` — wearpact.com optOut now records 1 click (close button) instead of 0; weathertech.com unchanged. 3. Visit https://wearpact.com/ from a US IP: the Osano bar at the bottom is dismissed via the close button.

body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215261535554316?focus=true ## Description: yachtclubgames.com renders a custom Vue cookie banner (`div.cookie`) with `Accept` and `Deny` buttons that no existing CMP rule matches. title: Add Dotdash Meredith CMP rule
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1214959942625055?focus=true

## Description:
Dotdash Meredith network sites (people.com, allrecipes.com, investopedia.com, etc.) use a server-rendered OneTrust banner controlled by their own Mntl.CMP wrapper. The OneTrust SDK is only loaded on demand, so the generic Onetrust rule cannot open the preference center or save preferences and silently reports a fake success while leaving the banner on screen.

Add a site-specific rule that takes priority over the generic Onetrust rule on these domains and opts out by clicking the banner close button. In consent-required regions Mntl.CMP intercepts the click, loads the OneTrust SDK and replays it, which results in OptanonConsent with all non-essential groups disabled and OptanonAlertBoxClosed being set.

> The new rule targets a broad set of `*.com` brands via `urlPattern`, pre-hides the OneTrust banner, detects the server-rendered flat banner, and **opts out by clicking the close handler** (then waits for the banner to disappear) instead of using the preference-center flow the generic rule relies on. title: Add zalando.co.uk to usercentrics-api test coverage
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215331530129962?focus=true ## Description: Reported as an unhandled cookie popup on `www.zalando.co.uk` in DDG mac desktop. Verified that the current `usercentrics-api` rule (post-#1338 fix) handles it correctly: the shadow-DOM `[data-testid=uc-deny-all-button]` click runs, the rejection is persisted (`UC_UI.areAllConsentsAccepted() === false`), and the popup does not re-appear on reload. Zalando is another heavy Usercentrics deployment (many vendors), which is the same class of site that motivated #1338. The previous `eval`-only optOut would dismiss the dialog via `closeCMP()` but time out before `denyAllConsents()` finished saving, so the popup re-appeared on every visit — which matches the original report. Adding `www.zalando.co.uk` as an extra spec entry locks in regression coverage for this case. ## Steps to test this PR: `REGION=NA npx playwright test --project=webkit tests/usercentrics-api.spec.ts -g zalando` — both optIn and optOut pass, with `selfTestResult: true`.

title: Add rule for Miles & More cookie consent popup
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215292887935230?focus=true ## Description: `miles-and-more.com` uses a custom Adobe Experience Manager cookie consent component (markers like `.cookieconsent__base[data-component="cookieconsent"]`, `.cookieconsent__buttonAcceptNecessary`, `.cookieconsent__buttonAcceptAll`) that does not match any existing generic CMP rule. PublicWWW shows no other sites using these identifiers, so a site-specific rule is the right fit. The new rule clicks `Accept necessary` for opt-out and `Allow all` for opt-in, then verifies the `consent_choice` cookie is set. URL pattern is scoped to `miles-and-more.com`. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. `npm run prepublish` 2. `npx playwright test tests/miles-and-more.spec.ts --project firefox`

title: Add tagconcierge rule for the Tag Concierge consent banner
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215341958592772?focus=true ## Description: theonion.com (and ~600 other sites per PublicWWW) ships the Tag Concierge `consent-banner-js` CMP loaded from `public-assets.tagconcierge.com/consent-banner/`. There was no rule for it, so the popup was unhandled. The banner renders `#consent-banner-main` → `#consent-banner-modal` (the bar) and `#consent-banner-settings` (the details panel). The reject button (`a[href="#reject"]`) lives in the modal on some sites, but only in the settings panel on others (including theonion.com). The new rule handles both layouts with an `if`/`then`/`else`: click reject in the modal when visible, otherwise open settings first and click reject there. The test step asserts `#consent-banner-main` becomes hidden, which the CMP script does on save. ## Steps to test this PR: `npx playwright test tests/tagconcierge.spec.ts --project=chrome`

title: Add independer.nl rule for custom cookie banner
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215358641230241?focus=true

## Description:

independer.nl uses a custom, site-specific cookie banner (`.ind-cbar`) whose reject button text is "Liever niet" — a phrasing not covered by the heuristic Dutch reject patterns, so the popup was being ignored by autoconsent.

Add a dedicated JSON rule that detects the banner and clicks the reject button, properly persisting the user's choice via the site's `Independer.Cookies.CookieUserAuthorisation` cookie.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish`
2. `REGION=NL npx playwright test tests/generated/auto_NL_independer.nl_ind.spec.ts --project chrome`
3. Load the extension in a browser and visit https://www.independer.nl/mijnindepender/inloggen — banner should be dismissed automatically.

> **Overview**
> Adds a **Netherlands-only** autoconsent rule for **independer.nl** so the custom `.ind-cbar` banner is handled when generic Dutch reject heuristics miss the **"Liever niet"** reject control.

title: Improve checkHeuristicPatterns performance.
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1163321984198618/task/1215327929738869?focus=true

## Description:
Improve performance of `checkHeuristicPatterns`. This function is called frequently on page load and, in the worst case, needs to check ~80 regexes on a 100k string. We can optimize it by always doing the minimal work:
 1. We only need all the matches when debugging the module, everywhere use we just check that `patterns > 0`. Therefore, except when logging flags are set, we can just exit as soon as the first regex matches.
 2. Likewise, we only need the actual matched text snippets when logging. When they're not needed we can switch to Regex `test` (instead of `match`) which is faster.

title: Improve heuristic detection performance
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1163321984198618/task/1215327929738869?focus=true

## Description:
The heuristic detector runs `getPopupLikeElements` which scans the DOM for fixed or sticky positioned elements. This is a synchronous operation that can block other page scripts, and affect performance on large pages.

This PR addresses performance issues by:
1. Only running the heuristic detection half as much (skipping the first detection iteration and every other iteration after that).
2. Bailing out of the tree walk if it takes longer than 10ms.
3. Ensure that the scan is at the end of the event queue, by running `setTimeout` at the start of detection.

## Steps to test this PR:


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Heuristic consent handling may run later or miss popups on very large/slow pages due to scan timeouts and running only on even findCmp attempts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Reduces main-thread impact from **heuristic consent popup detection** by scheduling work later, capping DOM scan time, and running the heuristic CMP less often during `findCmp` retries.
> 
> **Heuristic scan:** `getActionablePopups` / `getPopupLikeElements` now accept a configurable **`heuristicPopupSearchTimeout`** (default **100ms**). The tree walk starts returning `FILTER_REJECT` once elapsed time exceeds that budget so large pages cannot scan indefinitely. **`AutoConsentHeuristicCMP.detectCmp`** is **`async`** and **`await`s `setTimeout(0)`** before scanning so the heavy walk runs after the current event-queue work.
> 
> **`findCmp` scheduling:** The heuristic rule is included only when **`findCmpAttempts % 2 === 0`** (skips every other attempt, including the first). On retries, the code still waits **500ms**, but the **mutation observer** is only waited on when **`findCmpAttempts > 1`**, so the first retry does not block on DOM mutations.
> 
> Tests set **`findCmpAttempts = 1`** so heuristic detection still runs in the “no declarative match” case under the new even-attempt rule.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1a6ab069630a66379f976efb36a54bb6ea09ffff. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1215357412614455

> Adds a **`performanceLoggingEnabled`** config flag (off by default in the library, on for the test extension) that gates **`performance.mark` / `measure`** instrumentation along the CMP detection path.

title: Add Playwright HTTPS proxy testing skill
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1163321984198618/task/1215497097190950?focus=true ## Description: Adds a new `proxy-testing` agent skill for testing autoconsent behavior through HTTPS regional proxies in Playwright. The skill includes: - A concise skill guide at `.agents/skills/proxy-testing/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/proxy-testing/SKILL.md`. - A reusable library at `.agents/skills/proxy-testing/scripts/regional-proxy.mjs`. - A small AGENTS.md update pointing regional rule verification at the `proxy-testing` skill. The library provides helpers to: - Build Playwright proxy config with `{ server, username, password }`. - Launch Chromium through a regional HTTPS proxy. - Inject autoconsent into an isolated world via CDP, with eval snippets executed in the page's main world. - Test an existing page, one URL, or one URL across multiple regions. - Format test results and screenshot paths. Environment contract: - Regional endpoints: `REGIONAL_PROXY_US`, `REGIONAL_PROXY_GB`, `REGIONAL_PROXY_AU`, etc. - Shared credentials: `REGIONAL_PROXY_USERNAME` and `REGIONAL_PROXY_PASSWORD`. - Endpoint values are bare hostnames; the library adds `https://` and port `443`. - Chromium only, because isolated-world injection uses CDP. ## Steps to test this PR: - `git pull origin cursor/playwright-https-proxy-skill-fdb7` - `npm ci` - `npx playwright install chromium` - `npx prettier .agents/skills/proxy-testing/SKILL.md .agents/skills/proxy-testing/scripts/regional-proxy.mjs .claude/skills/proxy-testing/SKILL.md AGENTS.md --check` - `node --check .agents/skills/proxy-testing/scripts/regional-proxy.mjs` - Imported the library and verified `buildProxyConfig('us', env)` returns `https://:443` using `REGIONAL_PROXY_US`, `REGIONAL_PROXY_USERNAME`, and `REGIONAL_PROXY_PASSWORD`. - Verified `launchRegionalProxyBrowser('us')` with the provided proxy credentials via environment variables only; `https://api.ipify.org?format=json` returned proxy egress IP `128.203.210.198`. - Exercised `testUrl('https://example.com/', 'us', { action: null, completionTimeout: 2500, screenshotsDir: '/tmp/proxy-testing-pr-update' })`; it returned the expected `NO CMP` result and saved a screenshot outside the repo. - Confirmed no supplied credential values are present in the skill files.

title: Handle non-reject buttons in heuristic mode
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1163321984198618/task/1213990702372114

## Description:
 - Adds additional regexes so we can detect settings, reject and 'acknowledge' button texts in popups. 
 - Adds a configuration option to allow for heuristic mode to provide additional fallbacks when heuristic mode cannot find a reject button, and there is no settings button to indicate that reject is possible.
    1. Click a 'ok', 'understood', 'close' or similar 'acknowledge' button to clear the popup without explicit consent (tier 1).
    2. Click accept/agree or similar (tier 2).

## Steps to test this PR:


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Tier2 can auto-click accept on consent banners when no reject path exists, which affects privacy behavior; misclassified buttons could trigger wrong clicks on real sites.
> 
> **Overview**
> Heuristic consent handling no longer requires a reject button. Popups and buttons are **regex-classified** (reject, settings, accept, acknowledge), assigned a **tier** (Reject / Tier1 / Tier2), and filtered by a new **`heuristicMode`** config (default reject-only).
> 
> **`getActionablePopups`** takes a mode, keeps popups whose tier is at or below that cap, and sorts so reject-tier popups win when several are visible. Popups with a settings button are excluded (no auto-click). **`AutoConsentHeuristicCMP`** picks the click target from the popup tier via **`getTargetButton()`** and names itself **`HEURISTIC-TIER0/1/2`**.
> 
> New pattern lists (**`ACCEPT_PATTERNS`**, **`ACKNOWLEDGE_PATTERNS`**, **`SETTINGS_PATTERNS`**) and extra reject patterns (e.g. disagree, opt-out, abbreviated CCPA text) support classification. Tests cover mode filtering, tier detection, and **`optOut`** clicks for each tier.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fb2e7e00bf66c8a628282034882c1d78d38b4d10. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: ketch: handle US/CCPA preferences modal with no Reject All
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215605034286565?focus=true

## Description:
The newer Ketch banner uses #ketch-banner-button-secondary as a stable id for the 'Manage Cookie Settings' / Reject button instead of the older class-based selectors. On US/Canadian sites such as my.equifax.ca the preferences modal exposes only per-purpose toggles plus a 'Save Settings' button (no 'Reject All'), so the opt-out previously stalled and left the prehidden banner blocking the page.

- Add #ketch-banner-button-secondary to the secondary-button selectors so the modal can be opened on the newer Ketch DOM.
- Branch the preferences-modal step: if 'Reject All' is available use it (existing behaviour); otherwise toggle off every enabled purpose switch (input[role=switch][aria-checked=true]:not(:disabled)) before saving.
- Extend the confirm selectors to also accept aria-label='Save Settings'.
- Add https://my.equifax.ca/login as a regression test.

## Steps to test this PR:


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes consent opt-out branching across many live-site DOM variants; mis-clicks could accept cookies or leave banners open, but scope is limited to the Ketch autoconsent rule and tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Ketch opt-out** is reworked so more banner and preferences-modal variants complete instead of leaving the dialog blocking the page.
> 
> Banner handling now **prefers direct reject** via `aria-label^='Reject'` (so reject is not mistaken for “Cookie Settings” when button IDs differ), **confirms/saves** if a preferences UI stays open after that click, and falls back through `#ketch-banner-button-tertiary`, **`#ketch-banner-button-secondary`** (settings/manage), and single-button disclosure banners.
> 
> In the preferences modal, the flow **uses Reject All when present**; otherwise it **turns off every enabled purpose switch** before save. Confirm actions also match **`Save Settings`**.
> 
> Playwright coverage adds **Equifax** and **PBS** scenarios, drops **time.com**, and limits Ketch runs to **US and DE** regions.
>

title: didomi: avoid premature popup detection on aria-hidden hosts
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215529469878601?focus=true

## Description:
leboncoin.fr injects #didomi-host with a non-empty wrapper div but keeps it aria-hidden="true" until Didomi decides to render the popup. The previous detectPopup selector matched #didomi-host:not(:empty) unconditionally, so autoconsent fired before the popup was actually visible and called Didomi.setUserDisagreeToAll() while the SDK was still mounting, leaving the real popup on screen for the user.

Tightening the wrapper match with :not([aria-hidden="true"]) keeps the nothing.tech timing fix working (its host has no aria-hidden when the popup is rendered) while ignoring the leboncoin pre-render state.

Adds leboncoin.fr to the EU Didomi spec list.

## Steps to test this PR:


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small selector change in a CMP rule plus test matrix tweaks; no auth or core app logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Didomi `detectPopup`** now treats `#didomi-host` as visible only when it is non-empty **and** not `aria-hidden="true"`, so autoconsent does not run opt-out while the host is pre-filled but still hidden (e.g. leboncoin-style mounting).
> 
> **Playwright Didomi tests** drop `planet.fr`, restrict the main suite to **US and FR** (`onlyRegions` instead of skipping US), and keep the separate US CCPA site block unchanged.

title: Drop support for consent-o-matic rules
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201844467387842/task/1215492370899430?focus=true

## Description:
In recent coverage crawls, we now see no sites where consent-o-matic rules are active. We can remove this integration and instead rely on our own rules.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Removes an entire CMP execution path and bundled rules, so any site that still relied on `com_*` Consent-O-Matic rules will no longer be handled until covered by autoconsent rules.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Removes Consent-O-Matic as a third CMP rule format** so the engine only loads autoconsent JSON, compact rules, and code-based CMPs.
> 
> The **Consent-O-Matic runtime is deleted** (`ConsentOMaticCMP`, `lib/consentomatic/*`), and **`RuleBundle` no longer includes `consentomatic`**. The background script, standalone content script, and Playwright harness stop bundling or importing Consent-O-Matic rules. **`rules/build.ts` no longer fetches upstream Consent-O-Matic rules** or writes `consentomatic.json`; **`rules.json` and the rule index** are autoconsent-only. The **extension popup** drops the Consent-O-Matic rules section and related UI wiring.
> 
> **Docs and package exports** are updated (readme, API, puppeteer guide, `package.json`). **E2E specs** for `com_oil`, `com_quantcast2`, and `com_wordpressgdpr` are removed; native **quantcast** tests remain.

body:

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.60.0 to 1.61.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.

await context.credentials.create('example.com', {

id: credentialId,

userHandle,

privateKey,

publicKey,

});

await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();

await page.goto('https://example.com/login');

// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Browser and Screencast

  • New option artifactsDir in browserType.connectOverCDP() controls where artifacts such as traces and downloads are stored when attached to an existing browser.
  • New option cursor in screencast.showActions() controls the cursor decoration rendered for pointer actions.
  • The onFrame callback in screencast.start() now receives a timestamp of when the frame was presented by the browser.

Test runner

  • The testOptions.video option now supports the same set of modes as trace: new 'on-all-retries', 'retain-on-first-failure' and 'retain-on-failure-and-retries' values. See the video modes table for which runs are recorded and kept in each mode.
  • Supported expect.soft.poll(...).
  • New fullConfig.argv — a snapshot of process.argv from the runner process, handy for reading custom arguments passed after the -- separator.
  • New fullConfig.failOnFlakyTests mirrors the config option, so reporters can explain why a flaky run failed.
  • testInfo.errors now lists each sub-error of an AggregateError as a separate entry.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

> 
> The test extension popup swaps the heuristic checkbox for a four-option radio fieldset wired to **`heuristicMode`**. Library **`normalizeConfig`** defaults **`heuristicMode`** to **`off`**; the extension default remains **`tier1`** when unset.

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.

await context.credentials.create('example.com', {

id: credentialId,

userHandle,

privateKey,

publicKey,

});

await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();

await page.goto('https://example.com/login');

// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Browser and Screencast

  • New option artifactsDir in browserType.connectOverCDP() controls where artifacts such as traces and downloads are stored when attached to an existing browser.
  • New option cursor in screencast.showActions() controls the cursor decoration rendered for pointer actions.
  • The onFrame callback in screencast.start() now receives a timestamp of when the frame was presented by the browser.

Test runner

  • The testOptions.video option now supports the same set of modes as trace: new 'on-all-retries', 'retain-on-first-failure' and 'retain-on-failure-and-retries' values. See the video modes table for which runs are recorded and kept in each mode.
  • Supported expect.soft.poll(...).
  • New fullConfig.argv — a snapshot of process.argv from the runner process, handy for reading custom arguments passed after the -- separator.
  • New fullConfig.failOnFlakyTests mirrors the config option, so reporters can explain why a flaky run failed.
  • testInfo.errors now lists each sub-error of an AggregateError as a separate entry.

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

... (truncated)

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.61.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41365 [Bug]: Expect.Extend matcher with same name as default matcher in same expect instance overrides default matchers implementation to custom matcher
  • #41351 [Bug]: Playwright UI mode: apiRequestContext._wrapApiCall reports unexpected number of bytes (same test passes in headed mode)
  • #41360 [Bug]: Trace viewer: message times in websockets are downscaled by 1000
  • #41311 [Bug]: [Regression]: Sync loader throws "context.conditions?.includes is not a function" on Node 22.15
  • #41371 [Regression]: Sync ESM loader (registerHooks) fails to resolve extensionless .ts subpath imports across pnpm workspace symlinks

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

title: Add CNN Legal Terms and Privacy popup rule (US)
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216020381220615?focus=true ## Description: US visitors to `www.cnn.com` see a custom WBD-branded "Legal Terms and Privacy" modal that has only an "Agree" button (no opt-out option). The modal renders as a `body > div[aria-hidden="true"]` overlay containing a `div[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]` and locks scrolling by setting inline styles on ``. None of the existing rules detect this variant, so the popup goes unhandled in the US. This adds a cosmetic rule for `www.cnn.com` that hides the overlay and clears the body inline style to restore scrolling. The rule is gated on the `iframe[name="_usrConWBD"]` element (only present when the WBD consent system is loaded) and the specific overlay structure, so it does not run when the existing Onetrust rule handles the GDPR variant in EU/UK. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. `npm run build-rules` 2. `npx playwright test tests/cnn.spec.ts` 3. Visit `https://www.cnn.com/` from a US IP and confirm the "Legal Terms and Privacy" modal is dismissed and the page is scrollable. 4. Visit `https://www.cnn.com/` from an EU/UK IP and confirm the existing Onetrust rule still opts out without conflict.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the core detection path on large pages, so CMPs only reachable via generic/heuristic rules may be missed unless a site-specific rule matches.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **`maxDocumentElements`** setting (default **100000**, **0** to disable) so autoconsent can bail out of expensive **generic** and **heuristic CMP** detection when the DOM is too large.
> 
> In **`findCmp`**, site-specific rules still run first; before generic/heuristic stages, **`shouldSkipBroadDetection()`** counts elements via `document.getElementsByTagName('*')`, logs/sends **`autoconsentError`** with reason **`documentTooLarge`**, and stops broad detection (including retries tied to mutation waiting). Optional **heuristic text** scanning via **`detectHeuristics()`** still runs when enabled. The extension popup exposes the limit under **Other**, and performance reporting includes **`documentSizeCheck`**.
>

title: Update button patterns
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1215907159961593

## Description:
Add settings/accept/reject etc button patterns for other languages. See https://github.com/duckduckgo/tracker-radar-collector/pull/198.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Consent-button classification directly affects which controls get clicked; broader substring-style regexes and removed literals can mislabel buttons (false accept/reject/settings) on real CMP UIs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors **reject**, **settings**, **accept**, and **acknowledge** button matchers in `lib/heuristic-patterns.ts` from long per-locale string lists into fewer **multilingual regexes**, while keeping pay/subscribe exclusions on `NEVER_MATCH_PATTERNS`.
> 
> **Reject** coverage is broadened for EN (e.g. `but`/`except`, looser CCPA/opt-out) and for NL/FR/DE/IT/ES/SV/PL/CA/GL/EU via verb stems and “necessary-only” phrasing; DE explicitly **does not** treat `einstellungen oder ablehnen` as reject. **Settings** adds paired verb+noun patterns (both word orders) with lookaheads to skip policy/save/accept wording, plus trimmed locale-specific literals. **Accept** adds consolidated EN/DE/NL/FR/ES blocks (with lookaheads to avoid essential-only/reject labels) and treats more “save selection/preferences” strings as accept. **Acknowledge** adds multilingual close/dismiss and “ok/understood” patterns, with lookaheads so accept-and-close flows stay accept.
> 
> Tests drop two “except … essential / except necessary” reject cases, aligning expectations with the tighter `except … necessary` reject rule.

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

Network

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

title: Add Playwright integration test for bundled MV3 extension
body: ## Description Adds Playwright integration tests that load the bundled Chrome MV3 extension (`dist/addon-mv3`) and verify autoconsent behavior on privacy test pages. ### Changes - New `tests-webext/` folder with: - `fixtures.ts` — launches Chromium with the MV3 extension via `launchPersistentContext` - `helpers.ts` — popup navigation and banner visibility helpers - `autoconsent.spec.ts` — tests: - `index.html` — declarative CMP rule clicks reject - `heuristic.html` — heuristic detection clicks reject - `banner.html` — cosmetic rule hides banner; disabling "Apply cosmetic rules" in popup keeps banner visible after reload - `playwright.config.ts` — dedicated config for extension tests - `npm run test:webext` script - CI workflow runs webext tests after `npm ci` (which builds the extension via `prepublish`) ### How it works Tests load the bundled extension in Chrome and assert against `window.results` signals from the privacy test pages. The cosmetic test opens the extension popup at `chrome-extension:///popup.html`, toggles `#cosmetic-off`, reloads the page, and verifies the banner is no longer hidden. ## Steps to test this PR: ```bash npm ci npx playwright install chromium npm run test:webext ```

title: Add rule for DataGrail consent banner (fixes topps.com)
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216355620793985?focus=true ## Description: Adds a new autoconsent JSON rule for the [DataGrail](https://www.datagrail.io/) consent management platform. DataGrail is a widely used CMP (Topps, Linktree, Kong, Overstock, Bed Bath & Beyond, Earnin, etc.) that was previously undetected. **Root cause:** No autoconsent rule existed for DataGrail. Its banner is rendered inside a shadow root under `.dg-consent-banner`, so neither the heuristic rule nor any existing CMP rule matched. **Approach:** New JSON rule `datagrail.json` that pierces the shadow root using array selectors and clicks `button.dg-button.reject_all` (or `button.dg-button.accept_some`, which some deployments use in its place). When neither is on the initial banner, it falls back to `button.dg-button.open_layer` → `reject_all`/`accept_some`/`essential_only` inside the preferences panel. When the browser sends Global Privacy Control (`.dg-browser-signal-notice`) — a passive notice with no reject buttons — the rule dismisses the notice via `button.dg-header-close`, or finalizes via `custom` when a Save Settings step is presented (safe because GPC has already unchecked the toggles). Success is verified via the `datagrail_consent` cookie or the presence of the browser-signal notice (for GPC-honored sessions). The test spec covers the popup variants observed in the wild: the reduced initial button set exercised by the customize + reject fallback (konghq.com), the direct `reject_all` class with an "Accept Essentials Only" label (earnin.com), the standard three-button layout with custom text (getmyperks.com, linktr.ee), and the `dg-bottom` position variant (kindthread.com). ## Steps to test this PR: 1. Load https://konghq.com/ (banner shown reliably in EU/UK/US/JP). 2. Confirm the "We Value Your Privacy" banner is dismissed automatically. 3. Verify `datagrail_consent_preferences_s` cookie contains `dg-category-marketing:0|dg-category-performance:0` (etc.). 4. Reload the page and confirm the banner does not reappear. 5. Enable GPC in a Chromium build (`chrome://settings/privacy` → Send a "Do Not Track" / Global Privacy Control request) and load https://www.getmyperks.com/ or https://kindthread.com/. Confirm the "Your browser's opt-out signal is being honored" notice is dismissed automatically. 6. Same on https://www.topps.com/ from Japan (the originally reported site — behind Cloudflare bot protection so it can only be verified in a real browser).

title: Fix aliexpress opt-out and unblock detection on Polish pages
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216382528605680?focus=true Also fixes https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216386912390822?focus=true ## Description: The cookie popup on `*.aliexpress.com` was not being opted out. Three commits: 1. **`lib/heuristics.ts`** — `checkHeuristicPatterns` called `.substring` on every element of a `String.prototype.match` result. When a non-global regex has optional capture groups, `.match` returns `undefined` for groups that did not match, which threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'substring')`. One of the Polish `DETECT_PATTERNS` has this shape (`/(używamy|stosujemy|…)( są)?…/i`), so the exception fired on any Polish page. It bubbled out of `findCmp`, so autoconsent never ran opt-out — the aliexpress rule was detected on `pl.aliexpress.com` but no `popupFound`/`optOutResult` was ever emitted. Fix: skip non-string entries before calling `substring`. Adds a unit test covering non-global regexes with optional capture groups. 2. **`rules/autoconsent/aliexpress.json`** — AliExpress replaced the old semantic class names (`.btn-more`, `.btn-accept`, `.btn-save`, `.switcher-on`) on `#gdpr-new-container` with CSS-module hashes, so the previous opt-out selectors no longer matched and opt-out silently failed on every EU region. Rewrote the opt-out flow using structural button positions: - 3-button variant (most EU regions): click the second button (`button:nth-of-type(2)` = "Reject cookies"). - 2-button variant (e.g. Poland, which has no direct reject button): click "Personalize cookies" (`button:first-of-type`), wait for the `#voyager-gdpr-2025` detail modal, then click its last button ("Reject cookies"). The legacy `#voyager-gdpr > div` branch is preserved. 3. **`lib/heuristic-patterns.ts`** — added the `/g` flag to every `DETECT_PATTERNS` entry that was missing it. With `/g`, `String.prototype.match` returns an array of match strings instead of `[fullMatch, ...captures]`, eliminating the undefined-entry class of bugs at the source. Scoped to `DETECT_PATTERNS` only; the `REJECT/ACCEPT/SETTINGS/ACKNOWLEDGE/NEVER_MATCH_PATTERNS` arrays are used with `RegExp.prototype.test`, which becomes stateful (uses `lastIndex`) when the regex is global, so `/g` would be harmful there. ## Steps to test this PR: Verified opt-out and opt-in via regional proxies in `fr`, `de`, `es`, `gb`, `it`, `pl`, `nl` on `https://nl.aliexpress.com/`: all regions return `PASS` (popup found, opt-out succeeded, self-test passed). Reloading after opt-out no longer re-detects the CMP (cookies persist). Screenshots confirm the cookie banner is dismissed and the actual site renders. Local checks: - `npm run lint` — passes - `npm run rule-syntax-check` — passes - `npm run test:lib` — 829/829 pass (includes new heuristics test) - `npm run prepublish` — passes

title: TrustArc-top: permanently hide banner after opt-out shortcut
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216384796670938?focus=true ## Description: **Root cause.** When the `#truste-consent-required` shortcut is taken, TrustArc dismisses the banner via an opacity transition and only sets `display: none` from a `transitionend` handler. Autoconsent's prehide applies `opacity: 0 !important` via CSS, so when TrustArc's script sets `opacity: 0` inline afterwards, the computed opacity never actually changes, no transition occurs, and `transitionend` never fires. The banner is left in the DOM as an invisible full-viewport overlay (`#truste-consent-track`, `z-index: 2147483646`, `pointer-events: auto`) that intercepts clicks on the underlying page — the reported "login form not clickable" behavior on `admiral.com`. **Fix.** After clicking the shortcut, also apply a permanent `display: none` CSS hide for `#truste-consent-track` (and the legacy `.truste_*` overlays), mirroring what the fallback path already does. This guarantees the overlay does not intercept clicks even when TrustArc's own dismissal path is broken. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. `npm run prepublish` 2. Load `https://myaccount.admiral.com/login` (or `https://www.admiral.com/car-insurance`) with autoconsent opt-out. Verify the login form / CTAs remain clickable after the popup is handled. Test in multiple regions (US, UK, DE). 3. Verify no regression on samsung.com TrustArc test: `npx playwright test tests/trustarc.spec.ts --project=chrome --grep samsung`. 4. Reload after opt-out and confirm the rule does not keep matching.

title: Skip age-verification popups in heuristic CMP detection (doublelist.com fix)
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1214706429742001?focus=true ## Description: The HEURISTIC rule was clicking the **"I reject"** button on doublelist.com's age-verification modal, navigating users to a `Don't want to abide by Doublelist terms?` dead-end page (no listings shown). ### Root cause The age modal contains the sentence *"This site uses cookies for logins, ads and other normal site function."* which matches the heuristic's `(this|our) site.{0,100}cookies` cookie-consent pattern, and exposes a button labeled `I reject` (matches the English `reject` regex). The popup looked like a cookie consent to autoconsent, but rejecting actually rejects the age verification + ToS, not cookies. ### Fix Add `POPUP_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` to `lib/heuristic-patterns.ts` and short-circuit `getActionablePopups` when any pattern matches the popup's body text. Patterns target unambiguous age-gate / adult-content phrasing: - `age verification` / `age confirmation` / `age check` / `age gate` / `age restriction` - `over/above/at least 18 (or 21) years`, `18+` - `18/21 years of age`, `18+ years or older` - `I am 18+`, `I'm over 21`, `I am 18 years` - `you/users/visitors must be 18` (or 21) - `adult oriented/only/content/material/website` This is preferred over a per-site rule because the same age-gate + `cookies` mention pattern appears on other adult / age-gated sites — the heuristic fix prevents the same class of breakage without requiring per-site exceptions. A site exception for `doublelist.com` was previously merged in [privacy-configuration#5137](https://github.com/duckduckgo/privacy-configuration/pull/5137). Once this lands the exception becomes a no-op (HEURISTIC will no longer touch the modal), so no additional configuration change is required. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. `npm ci && npm run prepublish` 2. `npm run lint` — passes. 3. `npm run test:lib` — 837 tests pass, including new `isExcludedPopup` unit tests and the `popup-age-gate` integration case in `tests-wtr/heuristics/get-actionable-popups.{html,ts}`. 4. Local end-to-end verification with a page that reproduces the doublelist age modal: - Before fix: `cmpsDetected: ["HEURISTIC-REJECT"]`, autoconsent clicked "I reject". - After fix: `cmpsDetected: []`, popup untouched. 5. A normal cookie banner (`We use cookies … Accept All / Reject All`) is still handled as HEURISTIC-REJECT — no regression. Note: live doublelist.com pages are behind Cloudflare's managed challenge, so proxy-based Playwright verification against the production site was not possible in this task. Reproduction / verification was done locally against a page that mirrors the doublelist age modal, and the fix mirrors PR #1350 which included live proxy verification.

title: Add rule for abetterrouteplanner.com
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216427572851274?focus=true ## Description: abetterrouteplanner.com is a React Native Web app that renders its own bespoke cookie banner with Customize / Reject / Accept buttons. The heuristic rule doesn't pick it up, so autoconsent leaves the popup untouched in every region tested (US, GB, DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, PL, SE, DK, NO, CH, AU, JP). The Reject and Accept buttons expose stable `data-testid="cookies_reject"` and `data-testid="cookies_ok_all"` attributes. The rest of the DOM only uses framework-generated hashed classes, so there's no realistic generic pattern to hook into. A narrow site-specific rule keyed on those testids is the cleanest fix. Consent state is persisted via IndexedDB (localforage), and the popup does not reappear after dismissal + reload — no false-positive risk. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. `npm run build-rules` 2. `npx playwright test tests/abetterrouteplanner.spec.ts` 3. Load https://abetterrouteplanner.com in the extension build and confirm the cookie banner is dismissed automatically.

title: Add aa-cookie-banner rule for American Airlines properties
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1211364697371409?focus=true ## Description: aa.com (and its sibling properties envoyair.com, psaairlines.com) render a `` custom element whose shadow-root notice offers only a **Dismiss** button — there is no reject, settings, or preferences button. Heuristic detection missed it because the button lives inside a shadow root and "Dismiss" isn't a reject keyword. The new rule: - scopes to the three known American Airlines domains via `urlPattern` - `detectCmp` pierces the shadow root and requires both the host and `#cookie-banner` toast, so aa.com's EU/GB locales (which fall back to OneTrust) are not falsely matched - clicks `#toast-dismiss-button` for both optIn and optOut (the only action offered), which sets `cookie_banner=closed` so the popup does not reappear on reload - self-tests via `cookieContains: "cookie_banner=closed"` Labels to apply after creation: `category: rules`, `version: minor`. ## Steps to test this PR: - `npm run lint && npm run test:lib` - `npm run build-rules && npm run prepublish` - Visit https://www.aa.com/ with a mobile Chrome UA from a US region and confirm the "Privacy and cookies" toast is dismissed and `cookie_banner=closed` is set - Repeat for https://www.envoyair.com/ and https://www.psaairlines.com/ - Reload and confirm the banner does not reappear - Visit aa.com from an EU region and confirm the existing OneTrust rule still handles it (no cross-detection)

v1.61.0

🔑 WebAuthn passkeys

New Credentials virtual authenticator, available via browserContext.credentials, lets tests register passkeys and answer navigator.credentials.create() / navigator.credentials.get() ceremonies in the page — no real hardware key required, works in all browsers:

const context = await browser.newContext();

// Seed a passkey your backend provisioned for a test user.
await context.credentials.create('example.com', {
id: credentialId,
userHandle,
privateKey,
publicKey,
});
await context.credentials.install();


const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com/login');
// The page's navigator.credentials.get() is answered with the seeded passkey.

You can also let the app register a passkey once in a setup test, read it back with credentials.get(), and seed it into later tests — see Credentials for details.

🗃️ Web Storage

New WebStorage API, available via page.localStorage and page.sessionStorage, reads and writes the page's storage for the current origin:

await page.localStorage.setItem('token', 'abc');
const token = await page.localStorage.getItem('token');
const items = await page.sessionStorage.items();

New APIs

Network

  • apiResponse.securityDetails() and apiResponse.serverAddr() mirror the browser-side response.securityDetails() and response.serverAddr().

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.1
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

Markdown: Cap ordered list mark at 999,999,999 (#19351 by @​tats-u)

CommonMark parsers only support ordered list item numbers up to 999,999,999.

With this change, Prettier now caps the ordered list item number at 999,999,999 to ensure that the output is correctly parsed as an ordered list by CommonMark parsers. Numbers larger than 999,999,999 are not parsed as list item numbers and are left unchanged in the output:

999999998. text
999999999. text
999999999. text
999999999. text


1234567890123456789012) text

title: Add unive.nl cookie banner rule
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1214153980240662?focus=true ## Description: Univé's custom cookie banner is built on top of Tealium, so the generic Tealium rule detects it and calls `utag.gdpr.setConsentValue(false)` + CSS-hides the container. That is not enough: Univé's own close handler is what strips `body.no-scroll` (setting `overflow: hidden`) and what persists the reject choice. Without it, the popup visually disappears but wheel/touch scrolling stays blocked and the site later reverts the programmatic consent back to accepted. Autoconsent's own self-test happens quickly enough to still report success, hiding the regression. This adds a site-specific rule for `unive.nl` (all subdomains) that clicks the actual "Weiger alle cookies" button (`#no-consent-popup-close-modal`) directly. That triggers Univé's own handler, which persists the choice, removes `no-scroll` from the body, and cleans up the container. The Univé selectors are unique to this site family (PublicWWW returns zero hits elsewhere), so a site-specific rule is the right shape. ## Steps to test this PR: 1. Run `npm run build-rules && REGION=NL npx playwright test tests/unive-nl.spec.ts --project=chrome` — all 6 tests pass. 2. Visit https://rechtshulp.unive.nl/dossier-aanvullen from a NL IP with autoconsent enabled: popup dismissed, page scrolls with the mouse wheel, `document.body.classList.contains('no-scroll') === false`, and `utag.gdpr.getConsentState()` remains declined instead of flipping back to accepted. 3. Reload the page — the popup does not reappear.

title: Fix Our World in Data cookie button selectors
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216622582699366?focus=true ## Description: Our World in Data removed the `data-test` attributes from its cookie notice buttons, so the existing site rule detected the popup but failed to click opt-out. This updates the selectors to keep the old attributes and support the current stable button classes, and adds the reported grapher page to the rule test. ## Steps to test this PR: - `npm run build-rules` - `npm run rule-syntax-check` - `npx playwright test tests/ourworldindata.spec.ts --project chrome`

title: Cover old Reddit consent banner
body: Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216652699762932?focus=true ## Description: The Reddit autoconsent rule was scoped to `www.reddit.com`, so the same consent banner on `old.reddit.com` was not eligible to run. This updates the rule context to cover both `www` and `old` Reddit hosts while preserving the existing selectors and actions. ## Steps to test this PR: - `npm run build-rules` - `npm run rule-syntax-check` - `npm run prepublish` - Synthetic old.reddit.com check confirmed the `reddit.com` rule detects and opts out when the Reddit consent markup is present. - Live regional proxy validation attempted for all supported regions; Reddit returned its network-policy block page before the cookie banner could be served.

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.60.0 to 1.63.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API

Updates `esbuild` from 0.28.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

title: Update Dependabot config: ignore major version and set cooldown for safety
body:
Task/Issue URL: 
PR from dependabot https://github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent/pull/1442

I found the dependabot PR failed, It most likely due to major version upgrade, expected to happen in semserver.

## Description:

I added 2 changes, feel free to correct me if this is no DDG approach.

**Ignore major version.**
In Semserver, major version expected to have breaking changes.
Only updates the minor & patch version, and update major version manually.

**Set cooldown period**
I added cooldown ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-)) period for package updates to 5 days. This will allow the package to be scanned by other 3rd party providers in case it has chain vulnerability. Based from my previous experience, even the latest package could have vulnerability.


## Steps to test this PR:

None, if build green, that's mean package successfully built.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI/supply-chain config only; no runtime or application code changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Dependabot** for npm is tightened so automated PRs skip **semver-major** upgrades (`ignore` on `version-update:semver-major` for all dependencies) and wait **5 days** after a release before proposing updates (`cooldown.default-days: 5`).

> Major bumps stay manual; minor/patch and grouped dev-dependencies behavior is unchanged aside from the cooldown delay.

title: Dismiss The Guardian "consent or pay" wall in EU/UK via cosmetic rule
body: ## What The Guardian serves a Sourcepoint **"consent or pay"** modal in the EU/EEA and UK, where the only reject option is *"Reject all and subscribe to Guardian Ad-Lite for £5/€5 per month"* — there is no free reject. The generic `Sourcepoint-frame` rule correctly bails on this paywall (it clicks nothing), so the popup is left in place and blocks the page (scroll-locked). This adds a **top-frame cosmetic rule** (`theguardian.com`) that dismisses the wall by: 1. hiding the Sourcepoint container (`div[id='sp_message_container_...']`), and 2. removing the `sp-message-open` scroll-lock class from ``. ## Why this is scoped the way it is The Sourcepoint UI lives in a cross-origin `sourcepoint.theguardian.com` iframe, so the top frame cannot inspect whether a free reject exists. Crucially, the EU/UK consent-or-pay modal is **identical to the standard free-reject Sourcepoint modal** used in some regions (e.g. CA, JP) at the top-frame level — same container, same `sp-message-open` class, same `/index.html` + `consent_origin=tcfv2`. The **only** distinguishing signal is the Sourcepoint `message_id`, which is embedded in the container element id: | Regions | `message_id` | Reject option | |---|---|---| | EU/EEA (DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, PL, SE, NO, DK, CH) | `1482251` | consent-or-pay (paywall) | | UK (GB) | `1482252` | consent-or-pay (paywall) | | CA, JP | `1482255` | free reject (handled by `Sourcepoint-frame`) | | US | `1498198` | usnat notice (handled by `Sourcepoint-frame`) | | AU | `1418584` | global-cmp notice (handled by `Sourcepoint-frame`) | The rule therefore targets **only** `sp_message_container_1482251` and `sp_message_container_1482252`, and runs on the top frame only (`frame: false`), so it never fires in the free-reject regions and does not conflict with `Sourcepoint-frame`. > [!WARNING] > This is intentionally **brittle**: the `message_id` values are Sourcepoint campaign IDs and will need updating if The Guardian reconfigures the campaign. This trade-off is documented in the rule `comment`. ## Tests - New `tests/theguardian.com.spec.ts` covering the consent-or-pay regions. - `tests/sourcepoint.spec.ts`: Guardian moved to a region-scoped group so `Sourcepoint-frame` is only asserted in the free-reject regions (US/CA/AU/…). ## Verification (regional proxies, opt-out + screenshots) | Region | Acted CMP | optOut | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | GB, DE, FR, IT, ES, NL, PL, SE, NO, DK, CH | `theguardian.com` | ✅ | consent-or-pay dismissed; page scrollable (screenshots verified for GB/DE) | | US, CA, JP | `Sourcepoint-frame` | ✅ | new rule did **not** fire; genuine opt-out preserved | | AU | `Sourcepoint-frame` | ⚠️ flaky | pre-existing `Sourcepoint-frame` instability — reproduced **without** this change; new rule does not fire in AU | Cross-frame check: in EU only the top-frame cosmetic rule emits `autoconsentDone` (the iframe `Sourcepoint-frame` detects the CMP but bails on the paywall), so there's no double-completion / reload-loop. Compact-rule filtering confirmed the rule is present on the `www.theguardian.com` frame and absent from the `sourcepoint.theguardian.com` iframe. Local checks: `npm run build-rules`, `npm run rule-syntax-check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run prepublish` all pass. ## Note on policy Per `AGENTS.md`, consent-or-pay is generally treated as a paywall that "does not need to be handled" (the usual remedy is a `privacy-configuration` exception). This PR implements the explicitly-requested cosmetic dismissal instead; reviewers may prefer the config-exception route.

title: Fix Guardian scroll lock after back navigation
body: ## Problem On theguardian.com (EU/UK), the cosmetic rule hides the Sourcepoint "consent or pay" wall. When navigating to an article and pressing back, scrolling can break even though the wall is not visible. Two related issues were found with the initial bfcache fix: 1. **Race**: Re-running `optOut` on `pageshow` raced with Sourcepoint, which re-applies `sp-message-open` after our `removeClass` runs. 2. **Scroll reset**: Re-running `optOut` called `removeClass`, which toggled Sourcepoint's `position: fixed` body lock and reset scroll position. ## Root cause Sourcepoint scroll-lock uses **`position: fixed` on `body`**, not `overflow: hidden`. The previous fix targeted the wrong mechanism (`removeClass` + `overflow` inline styles). On bfcache restore, Sourcepoint's `pageshow` handler re-adds `sp-message-open`, which sets `body { position: fixed }` and jumps scroll to the top. Re-running `optOut` made this worse by fighting Sourcepoint asynchronously. ## Fix **New `stylesheet` rule step (version 3):** Appends idempotent CSS rules to the persistent `autoconsent-css-rules` style element. **Guardian rule:** Replace `removeClass`/`addStyle` with a persistent stylesheet override: ```css html.sp-message-open body { position: static !important; top: auto !important; width: auto !important; overflow: auto !important; } ``` This CSS survives bfcache, applies immediately when Sourcepoint re-adds the class (no race), and preserves scroll position because we no longer toggle the class or re-run `optOut`. **Removed** the bfcache `optOut` re-run handler entirely — it is no longer needed. ## Testing - Unit tests for `appendStylesheetRule` and `stylesheet` dom action. - Verified on Guardian GB: scroll position preserved when `sp-message-open` is re-applied after opt-out; scrolling works after back navigation + simulated re-lock.

## Description:
