title: Remove incorrect cosmetic flag from scmp rule
body:
## What changed

Removes `"cosmetic": true` from the `scmp` rule.

## Why

The rule was flagged as cosmetic, but its `optOut` performs a **genuine opt-out** through the Google Funding Choices modal, not just CSS hiding:

1. Click `.fc-cta-do-not-consent,.fc-cta-manage-options` ("Manage options")
2. Uncheck all checked consent/legitimate-interest preferences (`all: true`)
3. Click `.fc-confirm-choices` ("Confirm choices")

This writes a real TCF/Funding Choices consent-rejection state. The trailing `hide` step is only a fallback for the reject-less `GDPRBanner` variant.

A cosmetic rule is defined ([docs/rule-syntax.md](docs/rule-syntax.md)) as one that *"does not interact with the page, and only hide[s] the cookie pop-ups with CSS... useful for pop-ups that do not provide a Reject button."* SCMP's Funding Choices modal does provide a reject path and the rule uses it, so the flag was incorrect.

The flag was also functionally harmful: cosmetic rules are gated behind `enableCosmeticRules` and only used as a last resort (`lib/web.ts`), which would suppress this genuine opt-out.

## Verification

- Verified the live Funding Choices modal on scmp.com exposes the reject path (Manage options → 161 preference toggles, 42 checked → Confirm choices).
- `npm run rule-syntax-check` + `npm run build-rules` — pass
- `npx playwright test tests/scmp.spec.ts` — opt-out and opt-in both pass; engine now reports `isCosmetic: false`, `optOutResult: true`, `totalClicks: 3`
- `npm run lint` — clean

## Reviewer note

Regional proxy credentials weren't available in my environment, so I could not run the full US/GB/DE cross-region proxy sweep — verification was done from a single (GDPR/Funding-Choices) region plus the E2E test. The reasoning holds across regions since the rule performs a real opt-out wherever the FC modal appears, but a cross-region screenshot pass before merge would be worthwhile.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Single metadata flag change on one rule file; no runtime logic changes, only correct classification so the existing opt-out steps run in the normal CMP path.
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes **`cosmetic: true`** from the **`scmp`** autoconsent rule so SCMP is treated as a normal CMP, not a CSS-only hide rule.
> 
> The rule’s **`optOut`** path drives Google Funding Choices (manage options → clear consent toggles → confirm), which records a real rejection—not just hiding **`GDPRBanner`**. With the cosmetic flag, the engine could skip or defer this rule behind **`enableCosmeticRules`** and only try cosmetic CMPs after non-cosmetic ones (**`filterCMPs`** / popup handling in **`lib/web.ts`**), which wrongly suppressed a genuine opt-out.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 95273a1f30e9dfd1125418cc8659ee20fa22a8d9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: Fix regional proxy TLS chain validation with local relay
body:
## Description

Fixes an issue where launching a browser through certain regional proxies (e.g., `dew.socks.duckduckgo.com` for region `de`) fails with `ERR_PROXY_CERTIFICATE_INVALID` because those hosts don't send their complete TLS certificate chain.

### Changes

- **New local relay**: Introduced `startRegionalProxyRelay()` that runs a local HTTP CONNECT proxy on `127.0.0.1`. Chromium now points its `proxy` setting at this relay instead of directly at the region host.

- **Transparent chain repair**: The relay uses `connectRegionalProxyTls()` to establish TLS connections to the region host. When a connection fails due to an incomplete certificate chain (`UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE`), it automatically:
  1. Fetches the missing intermediate certificate via the host's AIA "CA Issuers" URL
  2. Retries the connection with the intermediate included
  3. Caches the intermediate for future connections to the same host

- **Secure credential handling**: The TLS connection to the region host always uses `rejectUnauthorized: true`, ensuring proxy credentials are never sent over an unverified connection.

- **Gateway support**: Added `connectRaw()` to support tunneling through `$HTTPS_PROXY` when set (needed in sandboxed environments like CCR).

### Helper functions added

- `derToPem()` — converts DER-encoded certificates to PEM format
- `fetchAiaIntermediate()` — fetches intermediate certificates from AIA URLs
- `readConnectResponse()` — parses HTTP CONNECT tunnel responses
- `connectRaw()` — opens raw sockets with optional gateway tunneling
- `tlsConnect()` — promisified TLS connection
- `discoverMissingIntermediate()` — probes a host's certificate to find missing intermediates
- `connectRegionalProxyTls()` — establishes verified TLS to region hosts with automatic chain repair

### Updated documentation

Updated `SKILL.md` to document the new relay behavior and the transparent certificate chain repair mechanism.

## Steps to test this PR

1. Launch a browser through a region with an incomplete certificate chain (e.g., `de`):
   ```javascript
   const browser = await launchRegionalProxyBrowser('de');
   ```
   Verify the browser launches successfully without certificate validation errors.

2. Verify the relay caches intermediates by launching multiple browsers for the same region and confirming subsequent launches complete faster.

3. Test in a sandboxed environment with `$HTTPS_PROXY` set to ensure gateway tunneling works.

title: Rule update: porngameshub
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1217743526538786?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

The banner is a notice-only cookie bar (fixed bottom aside, single 'Got it' button) that sets gdpr_consent=accepted. Heuristic detection failed because the same aside element also contains the adult-content disclaimer 'you confirm that you are 18 years of age or older', which matches DETECT_NEVER_MATCH_PATTERNS in lib/heuristic-patterns.ts, so isExcludedPopup discarded the popup despite the body text matching the cookie DETECT pattern /(?:this|our) (?:web)?site.{0,100}cookies/. I did not relax the exclusion patterns because that would re-enable heuristic clicking on genuine age gates site-wide; a scoped rule is the lower-risk fix. This is not an age gate: no reject/leave path exists, page content renders behind the bar, and the button is aria-label='Accept Cookies' inside aside[aria-label='Cookie Notification']. Rule uses those ARIA labels rather than Tailwind utility classes. optOut acknowledges since there is no reject option. No exception exists for this domain in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration (checked features/autoconsent.json and the android/ios/macos/windows/extension overrides). PublicWWW found no other sites with this markup (banner is client-rendered and absent from server HTML), so a generic rule was not justified. Verified no false re-detection: reloading in the same context after dismissal yields cmpsDetected=[] and zero banner elements. Stayed on the core region set per policy since results were consistent, the rule has no region-dependent logic, and it is site-scoped rather than a widely-used generic rule.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/porngameshub.spec.ts --project=chrome`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1217764864027240?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Custom bottom cookie notice with a single accept-only button (承諾する) and no reject/settings option; not a shared CMP (PublicWWW searches for the copy text, cookie__inner/cookie__button markup and the cookiesubmit cookie name found no matching sites). Heuristics do not fire: no Japanese DETECT_PATTERNS exist and the popup has no reject-like button. Tracking is not gated by the notice (GTM/GA4 load before consent) and clicking only sets cookiesubmit=1, so the click is acknowledge-equivalent. Key gotcha: the banner is visible from first paint but its jQuery click handler binds ~5s later, so a plain waitForThenClick silently no-ops; the rule waits for the site's app-init marker (#loader.is--show, added right after the handler binds and never removed) and retries the click if the banner is still visible. Verified no false-positive reload loop: after dismissal the rule reports cmpDetected but no popupFound. Banner only exists on the homepage; subpages have no .cookie element. No exception exists in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration for this domain (features/autoconsent.json and all platform overrides checked). No expanded-region escalation: core results converged, the rule has no region-dependent logic and no language-dependent selectors, and it is site-scoped.

title: Rule update: sex.com
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1217764122639837?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

No autoconsent exception exists for sex.com in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration (checked features/autoconsent.json and the android/ios/macos/windows/extension overrides), so this is not a duplicate fix. The reported dialog is a genuine cookie consent modal ('We care about your privacy' with 'Accept All' and 'Manage or reject Cookies'). Heuristics did not handle it for two reasons: the dialog embeds an 18+ disclaimer whose text matches DETECT_NEVER_MATCH_PATTERNS and suppresses heuristic detection, and the first layer offers no direct reject button. I deliberately did not relax the never-match patterns, since that suppression exists to protect real age gates. PublicWWW searches for accept-all-cookie-button, customize-cookie-button, confirm-settings-cookie-button and the site CDN sxccdn.com returned no other sites with this markup, so a site-specific rule is appropriate. Two implementation details: the modal is server-rendered and its buttons are no-ops for roughly two seconds until React hydrates, so both flows wait for body[data-scroll-locked] (set by the dialog's scroll lock exactly at hydration) rather than using a blind wait; and detectCmp is gated on html[data-cookie-consent-required], without which the rule kept re-detecting leftover markup after consent was already stored. Opt-out opens the preference center and confirms the defaults (optional categories default to off), storing privacy-preferences={"essential":true,"analytics":false}. A reload after opt-out produced no further cmpDetected or popupFound, so there is no re-detection loop. sex.com also shows an age-verification gate in some regions (visible behind the cookie modal in gb and de after opt-out); that is out of scope and the rule leaves it untouched. Escalation to the expanded region set was not required: the rule is site-specific, contains no region-dependent logic, and uses locale-independent data-testid selectors, and the four tested regions behaved identically.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/sex.com.spec.ts --project=chrome`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Adds an isolated site-specific consent rule and test; no shared heuristics, auth, or core infrastructure changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a site-specific autoconsent rule for sex.com so the cookie modal can be handled without relaxing global age-gate heuristics.
> 
> Detection is gated on `html[data-cookie-consent-required]` to avoid re-matching leftover markup after consent is stored. Opt-in/opt-out wait for `body[data-scroll-locked]` so clicks run only after the server-rendered dialog hydrates. Opt-out opens customize and confirms defaults (optional categories off). Includes a Playwright CMP test for `https://www.sex.com/`.

title: Rule update: bbva
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1217814051600992?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

No autoconsent exception exists for bbva.es in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration (checked features/autoconsent.json and the android/ios/macos/windows/extension override files). Root cause: BBVA renders its own AEM consent dialog (.cookiesgdpr__base with Aceptar/Declinar/Configurar) while also loading the OneTrust SDK, whose #onetrust-banner-sdk element is present but permanently display:none. Onetrust.detectCmp() only checks element existence, so the generic stage matched OneTrust and ended rule detection before the heuristic stage could run; autoconsent then waited forever for a OneTrust popup that never appears. Heuristics would otherwise have handled the dialog ('Declinar' matches the existing Spanish reject pattern). I did not change the OneTrust rule: requiring visibility in its detectCmp would risk breaking the many sites where OneTrust reveals its banner after the detection retries are exhausted. Instead added a generic rules/autoconsent/bbva.json that runs alongside OneTrust in the generic stage, so detectPopups() resolves on whichever popup actually shows. Selectors are anchored on .cookiesgdpr__rejectbtn/.cookiesgdpr__wrapper, which PublicWWW shows are BBVA-only (bbva.es, bbvauk.com, bbva.be, bbva.fr); a different flavour of the same cookiesgdpr component used by Spanish sites such as cata.com (.cookiesgdpr__rejectallbtn) is deliberately not matched, and cata.com was re-tested to confirm it still opts out via HEURISTIC-REJECT. Opting out writes aceptarCookies with all optional categories false; after consent the banner markup is absent on reload, so there is no false-positive re-detection (verified with a second page load in the same context). Spot checks: bbvauk.com (gb) and bbva.be (nl) both PASS with self-test true. No region escalation: the rule has no region-dependent logic and no language-dependent selectors, and the four core-set regions behaved identically before and after. Related site bundesliga.com shows a Contentpass pay-or-consent wall, which is out of scope and unaffected by this change. npm run lint, npm run rule-syntax-check and npm run test:lib (838 unit tests) all pass.

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Unsupported common CMP

The popup is served by STRIGHT, a consent management platform from Internet Initiative Japan (IIJ), loaded from cdn01.stright.bizris.com and previously unsupported by autoconsent. It is region-aware: under GDPR the first-layer banner exposes a Reject All button (which the existing heuristic rule already handled), while in jp/us/au/ca the first layer only offers Privacy Settings, OK and a close icon, leaving the banner unhandled. The new generic rule rules/autoconsent/stright.json clicks the banner-level reject button when present and otherwise opens the privacy-settings dialog and clicks Reject All there, using the CMP's locale-independent data-search-key-button attributes rather than visible text. PublicWWW shows the CMP on 100+ mostly Japanese sites (makita.co.jp, toei-anim.co.jp, yamada-denki.jp, tsukumo.co.jp, jprs.jp, nhk-p.co.jp), which justified a generic rule over a site-specific one. Escalated to the expanded region set because the rule has region-dependent branching. Reload-after-dismissal check: the CMP does not render the banner again, so the rule stops matching and there is no reload loop. body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1217942569159958?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

No autoconsent exception exists for postnl.nl in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration (features/autoconsent.json fetched directly and its 250 exceptions checked; no platform override match), so a rule fix was made. Root cause: PostNL rebuilt the cookie wall, renaming footer buttons from pci-button--primary/secondary to stamp-button--variant-primary/secondary, so the rule's optOut selector matched nothing and opt-out failed in all regions while the CMP was still detected. The footer now holds three buttons (Accept All primary, Adjust Settings and Reject All both secondary), so optOut targets the last secondary footer button and optIn the primary one; if the order ever changed the worst case is clicking Adjust Settings, which opens the settings pane rather than accepting. Two additional defects were fixed: (1) detectPopup checked visibility of the pnl-cookie-wall-widget host, which remains in the DOM after consent is stored and still passes isElementVisible because an empty custom element has a non-null offsetParent, causing a popup detection and opt-out failure on every subsequent load; it is now gated on .pnl-cookie-wall inside the shadow root. (2) The wall sets 'position: fixed; overflow: hidden; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.5)' as an inline style on body and its teardown is racy, leaving the page dimmed and unscrollable in roughly 1 of 5 runs; optOut and optIn now wait for the wall to disappear and clear body's inline style via optional steps (minimumRuleStepVersion 2). Breakage verdicts after the fix: leftover overlay none (no viewport-covering tinted element, no open dialog, no injected styles remaining); blocked scrolling none (body inline style empty, position static, overflow visible, programmatic scroll moved 500px); blocked interaction none (elementFromPoint at viewport centre returns page content ARTICLE.ptt-collo-details); reload loop none (popup not detected on a second visit in all 18 region/device combinations). Not a cosmetic rule. The regional proxies required --ignore-certificate-errors in this environment because the proxy endpoint's TLS certificate is expired relative to the VM clock; this affects only the local test harness, not the shipped rule. GDPR regions ch, no, it, es, se and dk were skipped as optional under the proxy-testing policy, since the popup and markup were identical in all nine tested regions with no divergence.

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

The popup is a custom 'Cookie' modal (NO / YES) injected client-side: div.cookie-modal.open > div.cookie-block with div.btn-box > div.btnText.simple-btn.cancel (NO) and .agree (YES). Heuristic detection finds the popup candidate but collects zero buttons, because lib/heuristics.ts BUTTON_LIKE_ELEMENT_SELECTOR covers [class*="button"] and not 'btn'-prefixed classes; the popup therefore classifies as 'none'. The button text 'NO' already matches REJECT_PATTERNS, so no heuristic-pattern change would have helped. PublicWWW searches for cookie-modal+cookie-block, 'btnText simple-btn agree', 'simple-btn agree', 'btnText simple-btn' and 'cookieLanguageModule' found no other sites with this markup, so it is not a shared CMP and a runContext.urlPattern-scoped rule is used. Opting out writes sessionStorage['cookie-disagree']='true' (nothing in cookies or localStorage), which is why the rule's test step asserts the modal no longer carries the 'open' class rather than using cookieContains. Side finding not fixed here: tlcbio.com, built on the same agency template (shared 'data-aost' signature), has a similar DENY/ACCEPT cookie bar whose controls are also div.btn, missed for the same heuristic reason; broadening BUTTON_LIKE_ELEMENT_SELECTOR to [class*="btn"] would cover both but is a change to a widely used generic mechanism and was kept out of this site-specific fix. body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1208026592770676?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Unsupported common CMP

No autoconsent exception exists for goodnightgoodluckbroadway.com in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration: I fetched features/autoconsent.json and overrides/{android,ios,macos,windows,extension}-override.json directly and grepped locally for the domain, with no hits. The popup is Farlo Consent Flo, a commercial CMP loaded from consent.farlo.co.uk via Google Tag Manager, so it warranted a generic rule rather than a urlPattern-scoped one. Reading flo.js showed the CMP's hide_decline_all config option defaults to true and omits the ._flo-consent-button--reject control, which is why the reported site shows only 'Cookie Settings' and 'Accept All'. The rule therefore clicks the reject button when a site exposes it and otherwise opens the settings panel, clears any pre-checked optional toggles (excluding the always-on --necessary one), and clicks 'Accept Selected'; in the script acceptSelected() with nothing selected writes the same consent state as rejectAll(), so this is a genuine opt-out and not a TIER2 accept. The self-test asserts ._flo-consent-root._flo-consent-hide, a class added only by hideModule(), which is reachable only from updateConsent() after consent is persisted. The task listed no related sites ('none'), so there were none I could not check; I nonetheless went looking for sibling installs of this CMP for the spec file and found two (everybrilliantthing.com and p3.productions) by rendering candidate sites and testing for ._flo-consent-root, both of which the rule handles (screenshots artifacts/sibling-ebt-us-desktop.png and artifacts/sibling-p3-us-desktop.png, verified visually). PublicWWW could not be used at all: every query, including a known-good control query for onetrust-banner-sdk, returned 'API available for paid search results only' with the provided PUBLICWWW_KEY. It would not have helped regardless, since Consent Flo is GTM-injected and never appears in server-rendered HTML, which is all PublicWWW indexes. Escalation to the expanded region set was not triggered under the proxy-testing policy: the core results converged exactly, the rule contains no region-dependent logic, its selectors are CMP class prefixes rather than language-specific or brittle structural ones, and it is a brand-new rule rather than a change to a widely-used existing one. Regional proxies required --ignore-certificate-errors plus ignoreHTTPSErrors for this host, which otherwise failed with ERR_PROXY_CERTIFICATE_INVALID. The reload-loop probe screenshot is at artifacts/reload-check-us-desktop.png. One caveat worth noting: the stored consent leaves cross_domain at the site's default of 1 because that toggle is not rendered as a checkbox on this install; it controls only sharing consent state across the operator's sibling domains, not tracking, and analytics, performance, and targeting are all written as 0.

## Description:

Category: Site-specific pop-up

de.readly.com 302s to www.readly.co/<locale>/offers, which is why the pre-existing readly rule (urlPattern limited to readly.com, selectors for the older .cookie-dialog popup on go.readly.com) never applied. Testing notes: the site is behind Cloudflare, which serves an interactive bot challenge to datacenter proxy IPs, so the harness had to run Chromium headed under Xvfb and retry until an unchallenged exit IP was drawn; separately, the regional proxy endpoint's TLS certificate (CN=*.socks.duckduckgo.com) expired on 26 Aug 2026, so Chromium had to be launched with --ignore-certificate-errors for any proxied run to connect at all. ## Description:

The VMock consent dialog's first layer exposes only 'Accept All' and 'Reject/Customize'. Heuristic detection matched the popup text (DETECT_PATTERNS hits on 'We use cookies', 'Accept All', 'By continuing ... cookies') but classifyButtonTextRegex classifies 'Reject/Customize' as a settings button, so classifyPopup returned 'none' and the popup was filtered out even in tier2 mode. The second modal contains a genuine 'Reject All' button, so the new rule clicks through both layers. Opt-out persists as the cookie user_cookie_consent={"essential":true,"analytics":false,"social":false}, asserted by the rule's test step. PublicWWW searches for "cookie-policy-modal", "manage-cookies-modal" and "user_cookie_consent" returned only unrelated sites, confirming this is VMock's own React implementation rather than a shared CMP, so the rule is scoped with urlPattern ^https?://(\w+\.)?vmock\.com/. No autoconsent exception exists for vmock.com in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration (features/autoconsent.json or the android/ios/macos/windows/extension overrides). The core region set was not escalated to the expanded set: results did not diverge, the rule has no region-dependent logic, its selectors are class-based rather than language-dependent, and it is site-scoped rather than a widely-used generic rule. title: Rule update: pandectes
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1218229278515894?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Pandectes' fadeOut() only sets display:none from a transitionend handler and skips entirely when the wrapper still has cc-invisible, which it does for the first fadeInTimeout (20ms) of the banner's fade-in. An autoconsent click inside that window leaves #pandectes-banner as a full-viewport, opacity:0, pointer-events:auto element at z-index 2147483647 that swallows every click while the page looks normal. Fix: hide #pandectes-banner after the opt-out/opt-in click (optional step, display:none !important). Because the banner is invisible in the broken state, the 'before' screenshots look like a healthy page; the load-bearing evidence is the elementFromPoint result and the raw-click test, plus the two annotated artifacts (swedishstockings-breakage-evidence-broken.png / -fixed.png) where the blocker is tinted red. 'Before' runs used 4-8x CPU throttling to widen the 20ms window; the breakage reproduced in us mobile, gb mobile and fr desktop, and stayed latent elsewhere. No autoconsent exception exists for swedishstockings.com in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration features/autoconsent.json, and none is needed. Residual note: the heuristic reject path (observed once on us desktop) clicks the same Decline button without the new hide step, so it could in principle hit the same race, but it only runs when no rule matches and the pandectes rule matches reliably here. Proxy runs needed --ignore-certificate-errors, otherwise every navigation failed with ERR_PROXY_CERTIFICATE_INVALID.

title: Rule update: scmp
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1215656287086181?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

No autoconsent exception exists for scmp.com in duckduckgo/privacy-configuration: the only 'scmp' hits in features/autoconsent.json are inside settings.compactRuleList (the bundled rule), the exceptions array has no scmp entry, and none of the platform overrides (android, ios, macos, windows, extension) or overrides/browsers/* mention it. So no PR or Asana task to print, and this is not a duplicate fix. Root cause: a detection race between the generic funding-choices rule and the site-specific scmp rule. In GDPR regions scmp.com shows both a Google Funding Choices dialog and its own bottom GDPR banner; when the dialog rendered first, the site-specific stage in findCmp matched nothing, the engine fell through to the generic stage, funding-choices handled only the dialog and reported optOut true, and SCMP's own banner stayed on screen. Reproduced over the nl proxy on the pre-change rule (scmp-nl-desktop-initial.png, CMP reported as funding-choices with the banner still visible) and fixed by making the site-specific rule detect either popup. NL was re-run three times after the fix and scmp acted every time. The report named no region, so the reported-region slot is null; the expanded set was run because the rule contains region-dependent if/then branching and the failure only surfaced outside the core set. The remaining GDPR regions (ch, no, it, es, se, dk) are optional under the proxy-testing policy and were skipped. The task listed no related sites ('none'), so no related-site checks were owed; separately, multimedia.scmp.com was probed as a possible sibling surface and is not covered by the rule's urlPattern, but it served a slide-to-verify bot wall through the proxy and showed no consent popup, so it could not be assessed - it is a different host from the reported URL and out of scope for this fix. The bottom banner's only control is a single ACCEPT (TIER2), so optOut continues to hide it rather than click it.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/scmp.spec.ts --project=chrome`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1214151811425253?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

The reported press-release URL 301s to https://news.massgeneralbrigham.org/; the same banner is served on www.massgeneralbrigham.org, so the rule's urlPattern covers both hosts. The task listed no related sites ('none'), so there were no additional sites to check and nothing to report as unchecked. Sibling Mass General Brigham hostnames found via PublicWWW for the banner copy (massgeneral.org, cooleydickinson.org, nwh.org, williamjames.edu-adjacent MGB properties) were opened and all 301 to massgeneralbrigham.org serving this same banner, so they are covered by the same rule rather than being separate targets. Site implementation detail: window.CC is undefined and Matomo/VWO cookies are set before any interaction, so no consent gating exists; the close button records cc_cookie in localStorage and permanently suppresses the notice. It is a dismiss/acknowledge control, not a TIER2 single-Accept button. Expanded region set was not needed: the rule has no region-dependent logic, is scoped to a single site, uses a stable data-attribute selector, and the core set results were identical.

title: Fix Sourcepoint scroll position restoration on back navigation
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1200277586140538/task/1218887485604242?focus=true

## Description

Adds scroll position restoration logic for Sourcepoint consent notices. Sourcepoint saves the scroll position before locking the page and attempts to restore it when unlocking. However, on back/forward navigation with bfcache restore, the saved position can become stale (e.g., clamped to the top after a page reload), causing unwanted scroll jumps.

This change:
1. Adds a new `EVAL_SOURCEPOINT_RESTORE_SCROLL` eval snippet that:
   - Restores the saved scroll position immediately (before Sourcepoint can use it)
   - Clears the saved position to prevent stale scrolling later
   - Handles the bfcache restore case by clearing the saved position on `pagehide` events

2. Updates the `sourcepoint-top` rule to call this eval step after removing the scroll-lock class

The scroll restoration uses `scrollBehavior: 'auto'` to avoid animation conflicts and only restores if the page is currently at the top (indicating a fresh load where the position was clamped).

## Steps to test this PR

1. Visit a site using Sourcepoint consent notices (e.g., a news site with a paywall)
2. Scroll down the page
3. Navigate back to the page and forward again
4. Verify the scroll position is restored correctly without jumping to unexpected positions
5. Verify normal consent interactions still work as expected

title: Document rule step traps for agents
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1163321984198618/task/1218179550237153?focus=true

## Description:

In https://github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent/pull/1567, the agent used `waitForVisible` + `negated` to wait for a popup to close. `negated` only inverts the final result, so the step fails at once while the element is visible. The correct form is `waitForVisible` + `check: "none"`.

This PR adds a "Rule step traps" section to `AGENTS.md`, with matching short notes in `docs/rule-syntax.md`:

- For "not visible", use `check: "none"`, never `negated` (covers both `waitForVisible` and `visible`).
- Array selectors search only inside the first match.
- `cookieContains` is a plain substring match, and cannot see `HttpOnly` cookies.
- `setStyle` replaces the full inline style.
- `npm run rule-syntax-check` does not check `rules/generated/`.

`docs/rule-syntax.md` also says that prehiding does not affect the visibility check.

It also tells agents to add new JSON rules only to `rules/autoconsent/`, not to `rules/generated/`. Removing a generated rule is allowed.

Documentation only. No code or rule changes.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. Read the new "Rule step traps" section and the "JSON Rules vs Code-based rules" section in `AGENTS.md`.
2. Compare each trap with the step code in `lib/cmps/base.ts` and `lib/dom-actions.ts`.
3. `npx prettier --check AGENTS.md docs/rule-syntax.md` passes.

title: Rule update: woo-commerce-com
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1218781783311574

## Description:

`woo-commerce-com` dropped out of the latest coverage crawl. It was already listed under `unsuccessfulSites` in the previous one. WooCommerce rebuilt its privacy banner:

- **Button classes changed:** `is-primary`/`is-secondary` became `is-style-primary`/`is-style-secondary`, so the old opt-out matched nothing.
- **Region-dependent buttons:** GB/EU get `Reject all | Customize | Accept all`; the US only gets `Customize | Accept all`. The rule clicks "Reject all" when there is one (the secondary button followed by another secondary). Otherwise it opens Customize, unchecks the checked optional categories and saves.
- **Buttons render disabled:** the banner shows its buttons with the `disabled` attribute for ~0.5–1 s, and clicks during that window are silently ignored. In GB the site also sets `wccom_cookie_consent_analytics=granted` on its own when the buttons become enabled. A too-early click could therefore look successful while nothing had been rejected. Every click now waits for `:not([disabled])`.
- **Self-test and detection:** the self-test now checks `wccom_cookie_consent_analytics=denied`, and `detectPopup` uses `visible` instead of `exists`.
- **Spec:** skips AU and CA, where WooCommerce shows no banner (the 4 failing tests in the first Jenkins run; the second run passed 0/14 failed).

The other CMPs missing from the same crawl (ef-ccpa, financestrategists.com, leafly, miles-and-more, pornhub-compact-cookie-banner, raspberrypi.com, theguardian.com) were investigated and need no rule change. Most of those sites serve a bot challenge to headless Chromium or show the banner only in some regions. theguardian.com was folded into `sourcepoint-top`.

1. `npm run build-rules && npx playwright test tests/woo-commerce-com.spec.ts`
2. Verified via regional proxies:

title: Upgrade Playwright to 1.63.0
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

Upgrades `@playwright/test` from 1.60.0 to 1.63.0. The bundled Chromium goes from 148 to 153 (Chrome for Testing).

Why: Cloudflare's bot protection on linkedin.com blocks Chromium 148, and launch mode makes no difference. On the same network at the same time:

| Launch mode | Chromium 148 (1.60) | Chromium 153 (1.63) |
|---|---|---|
| Default headless shell | blocked | passes |
| Headless shell, `HeadlessChrome` removed from the UA | blocked | passes |
| New headless (`channel: 'chromium'`) | blocked | passes |
| Headed (under xvfb) | blocked | passes |

When blocked, the page is Cloudflare's "Sorry, you have been blocked", so the LinkedIn rule never runs. Alternating 148 and 153 in one run gave 3/3 blocked and 3/3 passing. Chromium 153 passes even though it reports `HeadlessChrome` and `navigator.webdriver=true`, so the browser version is what Cloudflare reacts to, not headless mode. Other Cloudflare-protected sites are probably affected the same way.

Changes:
- `package.json`: `@playwright/test` `^1.17.1` → `^1.63.0`.
- `package-lock.json`: only `@playwright/test`, `playwright` and `playwright-core` change.

Notes:
- **Node 20+ required:** Playwright 1.63 needs Node 20 or later (1.60 needed 18). `.node-version` is 20.12.1 and the GitHub workflows use LTS. The Jenkins agents also need Node 20+.
- **Also in the Dependabot group:** this bump is part of the stalled dev-dependencies group PR #1442, which also carries TypeScript 7, mocha 12 and Web Test Runner 1.0 and currently has conflicts. This PR lands Playwright on its own.
- **WebKit and Firefox change too:** the bundled builds are updated as well, and I haven't tested them.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm ci && npx playwright install chromium`
2. From an EU network: `npx playwright test tests/linkedin.spec.ts --project chrome` passes.
3. Jenkins chooses E2E tests from changed rule and spec files, so it runs none for this PR. The full E2E suite was not run. Before merging, consider a broader manual run per browser (chrome, webkit, firefox).

title: Rule update: chatgpt
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1218386656211657?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Breakage mitigation needed

chatgpt.com shows its cookie consent dialog as a real `<dialog>` element. On viewports wider than 48rem the site opens it with `show()` (a non-modal bottom banner), but below 48rem it sets `aria-modal="true"` and reopens it with `showModal()`. A modal dialog makes the rest of the document inert, so prehiding it hides the dialog while leaving the whole page unclickable: the page looks completely normal but nothing responds to clicks, taps or typing. This was reproduced at a 700px-wide window and on mobile viewports, where the invisible modal held the page for up to ~1.3s per load.

This change limits the rule's `prehideSelectors` to the non-modal dialog (`dialog[data-cookie-consent]:not([aria-modal])`). The anti-flicker behaviour is kept for the wide-viewport banner, and the modal variant now stays visible until the rule clicks "Reject non-essential", so the page is never inert with nothing visible to dismiss. Verified across US, GB, DE and SE on desktop plus a mobile run: opt-out still succeeds, no consent cookie regressions, and the rule stops matching after consent is stored.

- `npx playwright test tests/chatgpt.spec.ts`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Upgrade dev dependencies and use Node 24.21.0 (latest LTS) everywhere
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

This PR does two things. No library or test code changes.

1. It upgrades every dev dependency that works with no code changes.
2. It moves all of this repo's CI to Node 24.21.0, the latest LTS release today, and regenerates `package-lock.json` with it.

It replaces the grouped Dependabot PR #1442. That PR fails `npm ci` because TypeScript 7 conflicts with the `typescript-eslint` peer range (`<6.1.0`).

### 1. Dependency upgrades

**Major upgrades**

| Package | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| @types/chrome | 0.1.42 | 0.3.4 |
| @types/sinon | 21.0.1 | 22.0.0 |
| @web/dev-server-esbuild | 1.0.5 | 2.0.0 |
| @web/test-runner | 0.20.2 | 1.0.0 |
| @web/test-runner-playwright | 0.11.1 | 1.0.0 |
| markdown-it | 14.1.1 | 15.0.2 |
| mocha | 11.7.5 | 12.0.3 |

**In-range updates (lockfile only)**

| Package | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chai | 6.2.2 | 6.3.0 |
| esbuild | 0.28.0 | 0.28.2 |
| eslint | 10.3.0 | 10.11.0 |
| globals | 17.6.0 | 17.13.0 |
| sinon | 22.0.0 | 22.1.0 |
| typescript-eslint | 8.59.3 | 8.71.0 |
| web-ext | 10.1.0 | 10.7.0 |

Transitive dependencies are also updated. `npm audit` goes from 52 to 22 findings (critical 5 → 2, high 25 → 3).

**Left out (they need code changes)**

- `prettier` 3.9.9: it reformats `lib/encoding.ts` and `lib/messages.ts`, so `prettier --check` fails.
- `asana` 3.x: it removes `Asana.Client`, which the release scripts in `ci/` use.
- `typescript` 6.x / 7.x: with 6.0.3, `npm run prepublish` fails (Node types are no longer loaded by default). 7.x conflicts with the `typescript-eslint` peer range. #1214 has the TypeScript 6 work.

### 2. Node 24.21.0

- `.node-version`: `20.12.1` → `24.21.0`. Jenkins reads this file through `fnm`. The old value came from the Jenkinsfile (#793) and moved to `.node-version` unchanged in #1448. On `main`, the dev tools already need newer Node (for example `eslint` 10 needs 20.19+, `ts-json-schema-generator` needs 22+).
- `checks.yml`, `release.yml`, `release-labels.yml` and the `setup-release-scripts` action now use `node-version-file` in place of `lts/*`. `lts/*` resolves to 24.21.0 today, but it will move to Node 26 when 26 becomes LTS. With one file, GitHub Actions and Jenkins always use the same version.
- Not changed: the `setup-node` steps in `ddg-release.yml` that use `current` or `22`. They set Node for the consumer repos (Android, Apple, Windows, extension), not for this repo.
- No `engines` field is added, so the browser repos that install this package see no change.

**Lockfile**

`package-lock.json` is regenerated from scratch (no old lockfile, no `node_modules`) with Node 24.21.0 and its bundled npm 11.19.0, which is the same pair that CI uses. I used `--before=2026-10-01T20:00:00Z` so that no version published in the last 24 hours goes in (for example `eslint` 10.12.0, released the same day). Direct dependency versions are the same as in the first commit. The newest version in the lockfile is from 2026-10-01 06:56 UTC.

**Not tested before merge**

`release.yml` and the `setup-release-scripts` action run only at release time. `release-labels.yml` runs on `pull_request_target`, so it uses the file from `main`. They use the same `node-version-file` input that `checks.yml` uses on this PR. The action uses the `autoconsent/` path prefix, which matches its existing `cache-dependency-path`.

## Steps to test this PR:

All of these pass on Node 24.21.0 with npm 11.19.0:

1. `npm ci`: passes, with no engine warnings. All lockfile packages accept 24.21.0.
2. `npm run lint`: passes.
3. `npm run prepublish`: passes. The `dist/` output is byte-identical to `main`.
4. `npm run test:lib`: 867 passed, 0 failed. (Locally I ran it as root with a config that adds `--no-sandbox` to Chromium. CI uses the default config.)
5. `npx playwright test --list`: all 1828 tests load. (Not run against live sites.)
6. `node --test .agents/skills/*/scripts/*.test.mjs`: 11 passed.
7. Optional: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`. CI does not run this check. `main` has 116 existing errors; this branch has 115 (the `markdown-it` one is gone, no new errors).

Also checked: `npm ci` with this lockfile works on Node 22.22.0 with npm 10.9.4.

body:
## Description

This PR adds a comprehensive benchmarking framework for evaluating the accuracy of the button text classifier (`classifyButtonTextRegex`) against a labelled dataset of real-world button texts.

### Changes

- **New fixture**: `labelled-button-texts.csv` - Dataset of button texts with occurrence counts and ground-truth labels (settings, accept, reject, acknowledge, other)
- **New benchmark utilities** (`button-text-benchmark.ts`): Shared helpers for scoring classifier predictions against labelled data, including:
  - Row-level and occurrence-weighted accuracy metrics
  - Per-label precision, recall, and F1 scores
  - Confusion matrix generation
- **New CLI tool** (`scripts/benchmark-button-classification.ts`): Standalone script to run benchmarks and generate reports
- **New accuracy test** (`button-classification-accuracy.test.ts`): Automated test suite that validates classifier performance against the labelled dataset
- **Minor pattern refinements** in `heuristics-patterns.ts` to improve classification accuracy
- **Updated test coverage** in `heuristics-utils.test.ts` with additional test cases
- **New npm script**: `benchmark-buttons` for running the benchmarking tool

The benchmarking framework is designed to be environment-agnostic (no Node or DOM API dependencies in shared utilities) to support both automated testing and standalone analysis workflows.

## Steps to test this PR

1. Run the automated accuracy test: `npm test -- button-classification-accuracy`
2. Run the benchmarking script: `npm run benchmark-buttons`
3. Verify existing button classification tests still pass: `npm test -- heuristics-utils.test.ts`

title: Export heuristic classification and DOM discovery for downstream use
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

Phase 1 of making autoconsent the single source of popup and button classification for tracker-radar-collector. This PR is stacked on #1604, so its base is `claude/elegant-edison-4l7tjh`. Retarget it to `main` once #1604 merges.

**New `@duckduckgo/autoconsent/heuristics` export**
- The classification code that doesn't touch the DOM moves into `lib/heuristic-classify.ts`. It's published as ESM (`dist/heuristics.mjs`), CJS (`dist/heuristics.cjs.js`) and type definitions. It contains:
  - `checkHeuristicPatterns`
  - `isExcludedPopup`
  - `cleanButtonText`
  - `classifyButtonTextRegex`
  - `classifyButtons`
  - `classifyPopup`
  - the pattern arrays
  - the `ButtonRegexClassification` and `PopupClassification` types
- The published type declarations have no imports, so a Node project can use them without the DOM lib.
- `classifyButtons` and `classifyPopup` accept any `{ text }` button. `ButtonData` now extends that shape.

**Page discovery available to other scripts**
- `dist/autoconsent.playwright.js` now sets `window.autoconsentHeuristics = { getPotentialPopups, getButtonData }`.
- tracker-radar-collector already injects this bundle into the same isolated world as its scrape script, so the scrape script can reuse autoconsent's popup and button discovery without a separate bundle.
- `getPotentialPopups` is now exported.

**Guard against DOM dependencies**
- `tsconfig.heuristics.json` type-checks `heuristic-classify.ts` without the DOM lib, and it runs as part of `npm run lint`.
- I checked that it fails both on direct `document` access and on an import that pulls in DOM-dependent code (e.g. `./utils`).

**Docs**
- Added a short "Heuristics" section to the readme.
- Updated the `classifyPopup` file reference in `AGENTS.md`.

Classification behaviour is unchanged. This PR moves and exports code only.

1. Run `npm run lint`. This now includes the DOM-free type check.
2. Run `npm run test:lib`, which includes the new `tests-wtr/heuristics/get-potential-popups.test.ts`.

title: Upgrade TypeScript to 6 and add a 7-day Dependabot cooldown
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

This PR replaces the grouped Dependabot PR #1605. That PR fails `npm ci`, because TypeScript 7 is outside the `typescript-eslint` peer range (`<6.1.0`). This PR takes the other two updates from it, upgrades TypeScript to 6 instead of 7, and changes the Dependabot config. It also makes the older TypeScript 6 PR #1214 unnecessary. #1214 also fixes `npx tsc --noEmit` errors that already exist with TypeScript 5. That cleanup is not needed for the upgrade.

### Dependencies

| Package | From | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| typescript | 5.9.3 | 6.0.3 |
| prettier | 3.8.3 | 3.9.9 |
| @duckduckgo/eslint-config | v0.3.0 | v0.3.1 |

- **TypeScript 6** no longer loads every `@types` package by default, so `tsconfig.json` now lists `node`, `chrome` and `mocha` in `types`. The other `@types` packages are imported where they are used. The declaration build (`tsconfig.build.json`) must now set `rootDir`, so it sets `./lib`. `ts-json-schema-generator` keeps its own nested TypeScript 5.9.3.
- **prettier 3.9.9** formats union types differently: since 3.9.0, prettier keeps a union type on one line when it fits ([prettier/prettier#18827](https://github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/18827)). With the new version, `prettier --check` (part of `npm run lint`) fails on `lib/encoding.ts` and `lib/messages.ts`, so this PR reformats them. Only whitespace changes, and our prettier config is the same.
- **eslint-config v0.3.1** only changes release tooling in that repo. No ESLint rules change.

I updated the lockfile in place with npm 11.19.0, the same npm that CI uses, so only these packages change.

### Dependabot

- `cooldown.default-days: 7`: Dependabot waits 7 days after a release before it proposes a version update. Before, it waited 3 days, which is its default. Security updates are not delayed.
- Ignore `typescript` `>=7`. TypeScript 7.0 ships without a compiler API, so `typescript-eslint` and `ts-node` cannot use it. When `typescript-eslint` supports TypeScript 7 (typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint#10940), we remove this ignore and replace `ts-node`, which will not get TypeScript 7 support.

### Library impact

None. The 25 generated type declaration files in `dist/types` are identical to the ones TypeScript 5.9.3 generates. The bundles are built with esbuild, which does not use the `typescript` package.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm ci` (this also runs `prepublish`)
2. `npm run lint`
3. `npm run test:lib`

I ran these locally with Node 24.16.0 and npm 11.19.0. All of them pass, and `test:lib` has 867 passed, 0 failed. I also checked:

- `npx tsc --noEmit` prints the same output as with TypeScript 5.9.3. That check already fails on `main`, and CI does not run it.
- The `ts-node` scripts type-check and run with TypeScript 6. I ran `check-pr-release-labels` with labels passed on the command line (no GitHub API), and the usage or `--help` output of `bundle-config-rules` and `get-text-for-xpath`.

Not tested: the Dependabot config change. It takes effect after merge.

title: Use needs-code-update label and stop label events from cancelling the labeler
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

PR #1608 did not get the path-based code-update label. There were two causes:

1. **The labeler run was cancelled.** The `Release Labels` workflow runs the labeler only on `opened`, `reopened` and `ready_for_review`. The workflow also has one concurrency group per PR with `cancel-in-progress: true`. The triage bot opened #1608 and then added two labels a few seconds later. Each `labeled` event started a new run, and the new runs cancelled the `opened` run before it got a runner. The run that completed skipped the labeler step.
2. **Two labels had the same meaning.** `.github/labeler.yml` used `code-update-needed`. People and the triage bot use `needs-code-update`.

Changes:

- Move `actions/labeler` into a new `path-labels` job with no concurrency group, so a `labeled` event cannot cancel it.
- Keep the per-PR concurrency group on the `release-labels` check job only. This job runs after `path-labels`, and also when `path-labels` is skipped or fails. So the check sees the labels that the labeler adds.
- Use `needs-code-update` in `.github/labeler.yml` and `package.json`. Set its color in `package.json` to match the label on GitHub.

Done outside this PR:

- Moved #1604 and #1606 from `code-update-needed` to `needs-code-update`.

To do after merge:

- Delete the `code-update-needed` label. Until this PR merges, `main` uses the old name, and the labeler would create the label again.

## Steps to test this PR:

GitHub runs `pull_request_target` workflows from the base branch, so this PR runs the old workflow. Prettier passes on the changed YAML files. After merge:

1. Open a PR that changes a file in `lib/`, then add a label in the first few seconds.
2. Check that the `path-labels` job completes and adds `needs-code-update`.
3. Check that the `release-labels` job runs after `path-labels` and checks only the version and category labels.

title: Don't wait for a DOM mutation after an attempt that skipped the heuristic
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219155926371446?focus=true

## Description:

Since #1381, the heuristic CMP only runs on even `findCmp` attempts. But the retry still waits for a DOM mutation (from #721 / #741) after odd attempts. That wait assumes every attempt has already run every detector on the current DOM, which stopped being true for odd attempts in #1381.

Failure mode: a popup that only the heuristic matches appears late, and its rendering wakes an odd attempt. That attempt skips the heuristic and finds nothing. The page then goes quiet, so the next (even) attempt waits for another, unrelated mutation. If none comes within 60s, detection gives up for good. #1381 added `findCmpAttempts > 1` for exactly this reason (see [this review thread](https://github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent/pull/1381#discussion_r3361416899)), but it only covers the first attempt.

Fix: skip the mutation wait after any attempt where the heuristic is enabled but was skipped. No precision is lost: an odd attempt only starts after a mutation the heuristic hasn't seen yet. When the heuristic is off, behaviour is unchanged.

Found on lego.com/en-us. The consent modal only opens after the visitor passes the LEGO.com / Play Zone age gate, and no rule matches it yet; that rule comes in a separate PR. Results, through Oxylabs DE, with the visitor clicking Continue after about 5s:
- **`main`:** detection stopped at attempt 5 in 2 of 4 runs, and the modal stayed open until a reload.
- **This branch:** in 6 of 6 runs detection kept going and the heuristic ran. In 4 of them it caught the modal right after Continue. In the other 2 it clicked Reject All during the brief moment the modal shows at load, before the age gate replaces it. That rejection is saved, but LEGO reopens the modal after Continue anyway. The rule PR handles that site quirk.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npm run test:lib`. The new `find-cmp` test fails on `main` (detection is still waiting after 5s) and passes here.
- Optional: on a page where a heuristic-only popup is shown after load and the page then stays quiet, detection should no longer stall.

title: Add rule for the LEGO.com consent modal
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219155926371446?focus=true

## Description:

Adds a site-specific rule for LEGO.com's own "Privacy preferences" modal. Reject All is `[data-test="cookie-necessary-button"]`; its label changes with the locale ("Reject All" / "Just Necessary" / "Nur notwendige"), the `data-test` attributes don't. Until now only the heuristic handled this modal (see #1611 for a detection stall it hit here).

**Why site-specific:** it's a component of LEGO's own Next.js app, not a shared CMP.
- PublicWWW has no hits for its markers (`ConsentModal_consent-modal`, `LEGO_COOKIE_SETTINGS`, `age-gate-grown-up-cta`). `cookie-necessary-button` alone matches unrelated sites, so a generic rule on it would be too broad.
- Other LEGO properties use different popups and are not covered: education.lego.com (hashed classes, no stable attributes), ideas.lego.com and kids.lego.com (OK-only notices). `urlPattern` is limited to `www.lego.com`.

**The age gate:** on a first visit, the LEGO.com / Play Zone age gate interacts with the modal. The rule never clicks the gate; it is out of scope.
- The modal opens on load, and 60–260 ms later the age gate replaces it (the modal is unmounted, not hidden behind the gate).
- When the visitor clicks Continue, the site reopens the modal unconditionally, even if a choice was already saved.
- So a Reject All in that short window saves the choice, but the visitor sees the modal again after Continue.

**How `optOut` handles it:**
1. Click Reject All.
2. If there's no `AGE_GATE` cookie yet (first visit), wait up to 1s for the age gate.
3. If the gate is up, wait up to 30s for the visitor to pass it, then reject the reopened modal. This part is optional, because the choice is already saved after step 1.

**GPC:** with GPC on (the DDG default), LEGO doesn't open the modal on load. It saves necessary-only preferences itself, so for DDG users the modal only shows after Continue on a first visit. The self-test cookie check passes trivially with GPC, but the modal is still shown and still needs closing.

## Steps to test this PR:

Our regional proxies, and a direct connection, get an interactive Cloudflare challenge on lego.com, so testing was done through Oxylabs. **The Jenkins E2E run will probably hit the same wall.**

`tests/lego.spec.ts` uses privacy-policy pages, which LEGO serves without the age gate. The homepage's modal depends on a human passing the gate.

Results (Oxylabs, core regions US / GB / DE, plus DE mobile):

| Scenario | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Homepage, first visit; simulated visitor clicks Continue after 3s or 10s | 12 desktop + 2 DE mobile | All pass: modal closed after Continue, rejection saved, no match after reload. 8 of 12 desktop runs caught the modal in the short window and rejected it again after the reopen. |
| Same, with GPC | 4 | All pass |
| Privacy-policy page | 16: 7 `testUrl` runs + 9 runs with a DOM timeline (US, GB, DE desktop; DE mobile) | All passed opt-out and self-test |

Notes:
- **Unexplained screenshot:** in one of the 16 privacy-policy runs (DE mobile), the final screenshot still showed the modal even though opt-out and self-test passed. The 12 runs after it (9 of them with a DOM timeline) didn't reproduce it: the modal closed within ~0.5s of the click, the cookie was set, and nothing reopened for 20s.
- **Remaining heuristic race:** in 1 earlier homepage run with heuristics on, the heuristic caught the modal in the short window one tick before the rule. That's a race within one detection attempt, and it's no worse than today.

title: Click Decline in the burpee.com rule when the banner has one
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1218886782247793?focus=true

## Description:

The `burpee.com` rule handles the Magento cookie notice (`#notice-cookie-block`). Some Magento themes add a Decline button (`#btn-cookie-decline`) to it, but on those sites the rule only hid the banner. The rule now clicks Decline when the banner has one. The Manage Cookies flow and the hide fallback for Allow-only banners are unchanged.

What Decline does depends on the theme:
- On some sites it saves the choice in a cookie, and the banner doesn't come back (cutmy.co.uk, workingperson.com, citarella.com).
- On others it only hides the banner and saves nothing (discountsurgical.com, lymphrx.com). There the rule matches again on every page load, as it did before this change.

The spec site list was stale: burpee.com no longer shows the banner, and knfilters.com and mossberg.com show automated browsers a bot challenge. The new list covers each variant with sites that load:
- Decline: discountsurgical.com, lymphrx.com, cutmy.co.uk, workingperson.com
- Manage Cookies: hobbies.co.uk
- Allow only (the banner is hidden): oxfordproducts.com, testequipmentdepot.com

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish`
2. `npx playwright test tests/burpee-com.spec.ts`

Tested from US, GB and DE:
- `tests/burpee-com.spec.ts` in Chrome and Firefox: all tests pass. With 4 workers, Firefox hit the 30s test timeout on discountsurgical.com and workingperson.com because the pages load slowly; with 1 worker they pass in 11–21s. WebKit was left to CI.
- Opt-out on the spec sites plus citarella.com and beautythings.co.uk, on desktop and with Android and iOS mobile emulation: the banner is gone, scrolling and clicks reach the page, and on sites that save the choice the rule doesn't match after a reload. citarella.com and beautythings.co.uk aren't in the spec because they block automated browsers in some regions.
- cutmy.co.uk and citarella.com lock body scrolling while their newsletter popup is open, with or without autoconsent. Clicking the site's own Decline button doesn't change it; on cutmy.co.uk, closing the newsletter popup releases it.

title: Tell agents to keep spec URLs current
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

Spec files keep pointing at sites that have since switched CMPs or dropped their banner, so their tests stop checking anything. Agents notice this while testing, but nothing tells them to fix it.

This PR adds one bullet to the spec guidance in `AGENTS.md` (Verification guidelines):

- When a spec site no longer uses the rule's CMP, replace it with a site that does, found in `data/coverage.json` or with the `publicwww-search` skill, and check the new site like any other.
- Don't just delete it: generic rules still need two sites.
- Check every region the spec runs in first. If the popup only stopped showing in some of them, adjust `onlyRegions` or `skipRegions` instead.
- For a site-specific rule, the site no longer using the CMP means the rule itself may be stale, which the existing "Updating existing rules" guidance covers.

## Steps to test this PR:

Documentation only. Read the new bullet under "Verification guidelines" in `AGENTS.md`.

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

This updates the generic `quantcast` rule. In the US, Quantcast Choice can show its "Do Not Process My Personal Information" (USP/MSPA) dialog (`#qc-cmp2-usp`) automatically on page load. The rule didn't recognize it, so the popup stayed open. The rule now detects that dialog and opts out: it turns on every opt-out toggle, clicks Confirm, and closes the success modal. The GPP usnat section then records Sale, Sharing and Targeted Advertising as opted out. Turning the toggles on needed an engine fix: a `click` step with `all: true` clicked every match back to back, and the CMP kept only the last toggle change. It now lets the page handle each click before the next one. Clients on an older engine still run the updated rule but turn on only one toggle in this dialog. Two existing races are fixed too: the rule now waits for `#disagree-btn` to stop being disabled before clicking it, since the click used to be dropped while the popup was still reported as handled; and it skips the "Save & Exit" step when "Reject all" has already closed the dialog. The spec's stale example sites are replaced with live Quantcast sites, and a US-only block covers the USP dialog (motor16.com, quotev.com).

Task/Issue URL:

title: oxylabs-testing: note what happens over the new-session limit
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

The `oxylabs-testing` skill listed the account limits (100 concurrent sessions, 10 new sessions per second) but not what happens when a script goes over them. Scripts that open sessions in parallel (a `Promise.all` of `withOxylabsPage` calls, or several scripts at once) easily open more than 10 in a second. `connectOverCDP` then fails with `WebSocket error: ... 429 Too Many Requests`, and the library doesn't retry. A CPM agent run and a follow-up OneTrust timing study both hit this, and a 429 is easy to mistake for a site result.

The Gotchas entry now says what the error looks like, that `testRegions` is sequential but parallel scripts are not, to stagger session opens, and to rerun tests that failed with a 429. Documentation only; no code change.

title: Check 'other' labels in button classification benchmark and fix false positives
body:
## Summary
- **Test coverage:** the labelled button benchmark (`tests-wtr/heuristics/button-classification-accuracy.test.ts`, `npm run benchmark-buttons`) previously dropped rows labelled `other` before counting false positives, so ~62% of the dataset was never checked. Those rows now count as false positives for the predicted label, and the benchmark prints an `other` section.
- **Withdraw consent:** revoke/withdraw-consent buttons (`widerrufen`, `withdraw consent`, `revocar consentimiento`, `retirer son consentement`, …) are relabelled `other` in every language, and the reject patterns that matched them are removed. We don't want to click these.
- **Label consistency:** manual label adjustments, plus alignment across translations (consent nouns and d'accord → accept, bare/only functional → reject, cookie policy links → other). Clear mislabels fixed (`avvisa`, `ukatu cookieak` → reject; `set cookies`, `pokaż cele` → settings; `masquer` → acknowledge).
- **Pattern fixes** in `lib/heuristic-patterns.ts` to reach zero false positives:
  - The settings noun→verb pattern matched the Dutch verb `kies` inside "cookies"; fixed, with explicit coverage for settings-noun + cookies phrases (`paramètres des cookies`, `ajustes de cookies`, …).
  - Exclude more policy/page links from settings; never match concatenated "accept all … reject all" text or text ≥300 chars.
  - Narrow do-not-sell, French `refus`/`uniquement`, and `accept all` patterns.
  - `dacord`/`daccord` move from acknowledge to **accept** (now tier2-only for single-button popups); `przejdź do serwisu` accept literal removed.
  - No regex lookbehinds, for older Safari compatibility.

## Results
| Label | Weighted accuracy before → after | False positives (incl. `other`) |
|---|---|---|
| settings | 94.8% → 94.9% | 0 |
| accept | 96.5% → 96.7% | 0 |
| reject | 97.1% → 97.1% | 0 |
| acknowledge | 96.6% → 96.6% | 0 |

With the labels updated, the old patterns had 26 false-positive rows (124 weighted), mostly rows labelled `other`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run test:lib`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run benchmark-buttons`

title: paypal: hide the no-Decline banner, retry the Decline click
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/414730916066338/task/1219330055492104?focus=true

## Description:

**Hide the banner variant without a Decline button.** Some PayPal banners (`#ccpaCookieBanner`) have no Decline button, only "Yes, I accept", a close button and a "Manage your cookies" link. They show in CA, AU and JP, and on `/ba/home` from any IP. For that variant, `paypal-us` followed the link to `/myaccount/privacy/cookiePrefs?locale=...` and `paypal-cookieprefs` submitted the form there. When the choice didn't stick, the banner came back on the home page and the two rules looped between the two pages.
- `paypal-us` now hides `#ccpaCookieBanner` when there is no Decline button.
- `paypal-cookieprefs` is removed. It only existed for that hop, and with the banner hidden the only way to reach the page with a query string is a user's own click, which shouldn't be automated.
- The banner is `position: fixed`, with no backdrop and no scroll lock. With it hidden, scrolling works and clicks reach the page (checked with `elementFromPoint` at the banner's position).
- PayPal sets `cookie_prefs=...type=implicit` (performance and functional on, marketing off) on the second page view when the banner is ignored. This happens without autoconsent too, so hiding the banner leaves the same cookie state as a user who ignores it.

**Retry the Decline click.** PayPal renders `#bannerDeclineButton` before its click handler is attached, and the first click or two are ignored. Because of that, opt-out often failed silently and the cookie stayed `type=initial` (seen in gb, de and on us mobile).
- `paypal.com` and `paypal-us` now click it with `retry: 10, retryInterval: 500`.
- The `paypal.com` self-test now checks for `type%3Dexplicit`. It used to check only that `cookie_prefs` existed, and PayPal sets that cookie on every visit.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `REGION=<r> PROXY_SERVER=<proxy> npx playwright test tests/paypal-us.spec.ts tests/paypal.spec.ts --project=chrome` passes in US, CA, DE and GB.
- Regional proxies, desktop and mobile (Pixel 7). Each run was a control load, an opt-out load and a reload in a fresh page:
  - **us, gb, de:** Decline registers (`type=explicit_banner`), and the banner doesn't come back on reload.
  - **ca, au, jp, and `/ba/home` from de:** the banner is hidden on both loads. There are no navigations away from the home page and no overlay or scroll lock is left behind.

title: Apply path-based labels only when a PR is opened
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

The `path-labels` job ran `actions/labeler` on `opened`, `reopened` and `ready_for_review`. A later run re-adds `category:` labels that the author has already replaced. That happened on #1642: it was opened as a draft, the labeler added four category labels, they were replaced with `category: enhancement`, and when the PR was marked ready for review the labeler added `category: ci` and `category: ai` again. The release label check then fails, because it requires exactly one category label.

This PR runs the labeler on `opened` only. Nothing is lost:

- `opened` also fires for draft PRs.
- Labels stay on a PR when it is closed and reopened.

The `release-labels` job still runs on every event, including when `path-labels` is skipped.

A PR that gets a category label right after it is opened, for example with `gh pr create --label`, can still get a second one from the labeler, as on #1627. The release label check's comment then says which label to remove.

## Steps to test this PR:

GitHub runs `pull_request_target` workflows from the base branch, so this PR runs the old workflow. Prettier passes on the changed file. After merge:

1. Open a draft PR and replace its category label. Mark it ready for review, and check that the `path-labels` job is skipped and no category label is added.
2. Open a PR that changes `lib/`, and check that the labeler still adds `needs-code-update`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Axeptio projects can delay opening the consent widget through the `delay` setting. It is very common: values of 3500–5000 ms (sometimes 8000+ ms) are typical. Autoconsent detects the CMP right away, but its ~5 s popup-detection window often ends before the delayed widget appears, so the popup is left unhandled (e.g. memo-de-vie.org, delay 5000 ms). This change adds a `detectPopup` branch that treats Axeptio's pending consent state (`axeptio_cookies` containing `"$$completed":false`) as an open popup. The existing optOut already waits for the dismiss button, and optIn now uses `waitForThenClick` so it also waits for the delayed widget. Once the user has made a choice the cookie becomes `$$completed:true`, so the rule stops matching on reload. Three delayed-widget sites are added to the spec.

title: Remove unused Dockerfile; match extension Node in release job
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1219118743429742

## Description:

**Remove the unused `Dockerfile`.** It is based on `node:12`, which reached end of life in 2022. It dates from the 2019 "dockerized puppeteer" experiment and was last changed in March 2020. No workflow, script or doc in the repo references it, and Node is already declared in `.node-version`.

**`ddg-release.yml` → `update_extension`: read the extension's `.nvmrc`.** This job runs `npm ci` / `npm install` inside the `duckduckgo-privacy-extension` checkout, so its Node has to match the extension's to avoid lockfile churn. It was hardcoded to `22`, but the extension moved to Node 24 in duckduckgo/duckduckgo-privacy-extension#3655. `node-version-file: extension/.nvmrc` follows the extension automatically from now on. The extension is checked out to `extension/` before this step, so the path resolves.

No library code changes, so consumers are unaffected.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `grep -rni docker --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude=package-lock.json .` finds only an old CHANGELOG entry.
2. CI passes. The `update_extension` change only runs during a DDG release, which should set up Node 24.x from `extension/.nvmrc`.

title: Test every region before relying on the heuristic
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

Adds one line to the "Updating existing rules" guidance in `AGENTS.md`:

> When the heuristic already handles the popup, test every region before concluding that no fix is needed.

The heuristic matches button text, so a popup it handles in one region can slip past it in another region's language. Testing only the core regions can miss that and lead to a "no fix needed" verdict. The bullet above it already covers what to do when the heuristic misses: extend `lib/heuristic-patterns.ts` for a site-specific popup, or write a rule for a generic CMP.

## Description:

Fixes the `cookiecuttr` rule for Presspage newsroom sites (for example news.keckmedicine.org, newsroom.odido.nl, nieuws.schiphol.nl and media.toyota.fr). Presspage uses cookieCuttr markup, but it also renders a hidden `#cookies_declinedbar` that contains a second `.cc-cookie-accept`. ## Description:

Adds a generic rule for the CCM19 consent manager (ccm19.de), a widely used German CMP that had no rule, used both cloud-hosted and self-hosted. title: Handle WP DSGVO Tools notice popup, replace stale sandhills rule
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1217354260753247?focus=true

## Description:

Investigated five rules that dropped out of coverage: WP DSGVO Tools, police-uk, sandhills, toyota and tplink. None of them regressed in code.

- **toyota, tplink:** spec sites pass in US/GB/DE. These rules only had 1–2 sites in coverage, so dropping out is sampling noise. No change.
- **police-uk:** all 5 sites show a Cloudflare challenge to our proxies. Tested through Oxylabs, all 5 pass in GB. No change.
- **WP DSGVO Tools:** ptk-hessen.de blocks our proxies. Behind the block it uses a notice-only layout that the rule never handled (see below).
- **sandhills:** all Sandhills Global sites (tractorhouse, machinerytrader, controller, truckpaper, auctiontime, equipmentfacts, marketbook.ca, rvuniverse) moved to Usercentrics, and `usercentrics-api` handles them (opt-out and self-test pass in US/GB/DE).

### WP DSGVO Tools: notice-only popup

Sites that process only necessary data show a popup with just "Ok" (`.sp-dsgvo-privacy-btn-accept-all`) and the ✕ (`.sp-dsgvo-popup-close`). Opt-out waited for `.sp-dsgvo-privacy-btn-accept-nothing`, which never appears, so it failed. That covers 6 of the 31 sites I sampled from PublicWWW. PublicWWW reports ~6.4k of the plugin's ~9k sites without that button, though not all of them render the popup.

- If "accept nothing" exists, opt-out clicks it as before; otherwise it clicks the ✕. The ✕ stores `sp_dsgvo_cookie_settings` with `"integrations":[]` and the popup stays gone after reload.
- `test` now checks for the URL-encoded empty integrations list. The old check (no `sp_dsgvo_cookie_settings` cookie) passed trivially on shop.fellhof.com, which is the vendor's Shopware build and stores `legalweb_cookie_settings`. The new check works for both builds.
- Spec: added 2 sites with "accept nothing" and 2 notice-only sites. Removed `skipRegions: ['US']`, since all spec sites now show the popup in US.

### sandhills → cz-eshop-cookies-consent

The `.cookies-consent .cookies-inner` selectors still matched 5 Czech shops built on one e-shop platform (`/js/cookies.consent.js`). There the cosmetic rule only hid a banner that has a real reject button ("Odmítnout", `.cookies-consent-accept-needed`). I removed `sandhills` and added a rule for that platform that clicks reject.

- Reject stores `cookiesConsentAllowedServices=[{"type":"technical",...}]`. Accept-all appends `analytical`/`marketing` entries, so the test checks for a single category.
- The platform reloads the page right after a choice, which cuts off the self-test, so `testSelfTest: false` (same as kasasmart.com in the tplink spec).
- `retry` on the reject click: on slow connections (US/AU/JP proxies) the click landed before the platform's jQuery `ready` handlers were attached. Nothing happened, yet opt-out reported success. The banner hides once the click is handled, so `retry` is safe here.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run build-rules && npx playwright test tests/dsgvo.spec.ts tests/cz-eshop-cookies-consent.spec.ts`. This passes locally in chrome and webkit (16/16 each).
2. Regional runs (proxies, after `npm run prepublish`), checked with screenshots:
   - WP DSGVO Tools: 15 sites × US/GB/DE/FR/NL/PL/AU/CA/JP. All pass except fotostudio-thomas.de in AU/JP, where the popup is not detected before timeout (slow load; that site uses the unchanged "accept nothing" path), and zuettl.com in JP (no popup).
   - ptk-hessen.de: DE via Oxylabs, pass.
   - Mobile sanity check via Oxylabs: vfc-plauen.de and shop.fellhof.com (DE) pass.
   - cz-eshop-cookies-consent: 5 sites × the same 9 regions. All 45 runs end with the banner hidden, the reject-only cookie set, and no banner after reload. Mobile sanity check (CZ via Oxylabs) passes.
3. Reload after opt-out: the popup stays hidden for both rules.

Fixes intermittent opt-out failures in the `toyota` rule (Toyota/Lexus Ensighten privacy banner, e.g. lexus.com). If autoconsent clicked "Cookie Consent Options" before the Ensighten modal (`#ensModalWrapper`) was injected, the site's click handler closed the banner and then threw. The preferences modal never opened, nothing was saved, and the banner came back on the next visit. The rule now waits for `#ensModalWrapper` to exist before clicking. Separately, when the site adds `#consentModalOverlay`, it attaches the handler that removes the overlay and restores page scrolling 300ms after the modal opens. Saving before then left the page unscrollable. So when that overlay is present, the rule now waits for the handler to be ready (signalled by `tabindex` on `#ensModalWrapper`) before saving.

Extends the `piwik-pro` rule to cover the newer Piwik PRO consent form, which uses `ppms_cm_*` element IDs instead of `#PiwikPROConsentForm-*`. Fixes a false-positive detection by the `automattic-cmp-optout` rule. Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.63.0 to 1.64.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
use: {
video: {
mode: 'on',
size: { width: 1920, height: 1080 },
fps: 60,
show: {
actions: {
style: {
point: 'width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 50%; background: red',
highlight: 'outline: 2px solid #333; background: rgba(0, 128, 255, .15)',
title: 'font-size: 16px',
},
},
},
},
</tr></table>
