title: Rule update: Tealium
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219676534765459?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Fixes a scroll lock left behind by the Tealium rule on mainova.de. The site runs a variant of the Tealium preferences prompt that sets `overflow: hidden` on both `html` and `body`, and only a click on its "Ablehnen" button (`#deny_full_submit_1`) removes it. The rule's fallback branch hid the dialog without clicking that button, so the page could stay unscrollable (seen mostly on mobile). This PR adds `#deny_full_submit_1` to the rule's existing optional list of decline buttons. Clicking it stores the rejection and removes the scroll lock. mainova.de is added to the Tealium spec.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/tealium.spec.ts --project chrome`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Rule update: Tealium
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219676520000132?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Fixes a scroll lock left behind by the Tealium rule on Tealium's consent preferences prompt variant (`#__tealiumGDPRcpPrefs`), seen on keurig.ca. The prompt's own script adds a body class (`overflowHidden`) that sets `overflow: hidden !important`, and only the prompt's close handler removes it. The rule set consent through `utag.gdpr` and then hid the prompt, so the page could not be scrolled. The rule now clicks the prompt's own Reject All button (`#__tealiumGDPRcpPrefs #preferences_prompt_reject_all_submit`) when it exists, the same way as the existing `#__tealiumGDPRecModal #rejectAll` branch. That runs the site's close handler, which saves the rejection and unlocks scrolling. The self-test visibility check now looks at the prompt's children (`#__tealiumGDPRcpPrefs > *`), because the empty wrapper div stays in the page after the prompt closes. keurig.ca is added to the Tealium spec (skipped for US, where the popup shows inconsistently).

## Steps to test this PR:

- `PROXY_SERVER=$REGIONAL_PROXY_GB REGION=GB npx playwright test tests/tealium.spec.ts --project=chrome --retries=1 (repeated with DE)`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Rule update: vd-ch

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219678809474570?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific `vd-ch` rule for the cookie notice on vd.ch, the official site of the Canton of Vaud. The notice is a custom Bootstrap alert (`.alert-cookie`) whose only control is an icon-only close button (`#dismiss-cookie-banner-button`). It has no text, so the heuristic cannot classify it, and no known CMP rule matches it. The rule clicks that close button for both opt-out and opt-in. The site then sets the `vd_cookie_warning=1` cookie, which the rule's self-test checks.

Adds an `educamadrid` rule for the in-house cookie banner used across the EducaMadrid education platform (www.educa2.madrid.org, mediateca.educa.madrid.org, formacion.educa.madrid.org and others). Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219678723533321?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a `gobiernodecanarias` rule for the custom cookie modal (`.cookie-consent-modal`) used on Gobierno de Canarias portals (gobiernodecanarias.org, gobcan.net). The modal has no reject button. It shows only "Aceptar Cookies" and an analytics checkbox, checked by default, under "Configuración de Cookie". title: Rule update: librus
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219678736308793?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific `librus` rule for the in-house cookie consent modal on Librus (synergia.librus.pl redirects to portal.librus.pl). The modal's first layer only offers "Ustawienia zaawansowane" (advanced settings) and "Akceptuję" (accept). To opt out, the rule opens the settings, waits until the settings app has rendered its category switches, turns off any optional category that is on (all are off by default), and clicks "Zapisz" (save), which keeps only necessary cookies. The wait matters: if "Zapisz" is clicked before the switches render, the site sends an empty category list and rejects it. Opt-in clicks "Akceptuję i przechodzę do serwisu". The self-test is disabled in the spec because saving reloads the page.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/librus.spec.ts --project=chrome`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Rule update: rabobank
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219678739974681?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a `rabobank` rule for the in-house cookie banner used across Rabobank sites (rabobank.nl, rabobank.com, raboimpactfoundation.com, rabobank.de, rabofinance.cl and others). The banner is the Angular `feature-modular-cookiebanner-variant-one` component, and its buttons are `rds-button` custom elements, so no existing rule or heuristic caught it. In the consent variant, opt-out clicks the "Weigeren" / "Only necessary cookies" button (consent level 1). In the notice-only variant, where the site uses only necessary cookies, it clicks the single acknowledge button. The banner is server-rendered and its click handlers attach only after hydration, so the clicks use `retry`. The spec disables the self-test because the site reloads the page after a choice.

## Steps to test this PR:

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific rule for MEGA's own cookie banner on mega.io and mega.nz (mega.nz redirects to mega.io). In GDPR regions the banner has a visible "Reject all" button, and the rule clicks it. The rule detects the banner by its reject button, clicks Reject to opt out (Accept to opt in), and checks the `<prefix>_consent=denied` cookie. ## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Newer versions of the lgcookieslaw PrestaShop module (the "lineagrafica" CMP) can show a "Reject all" button. The banner then carries a `.lgcookieslaw-reject-button-enabled` class, and some sites give it a hashed ID such as `lgcookieslaw_banner_<hash>`. This PR adds a non-cosmetic `lineagrafica-reject` rule that clicks the banner's reject button whenever that button is present. Non-cosmetic rules take priority, so it is used before the cosmetic `lineagrafica` rule. That rule stays as the fallback for older accept-only banners. The spec covers four sites with this variant.

title: Move tldts-experimental to devDependencies

Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

`tldts-experimental` is only imported by the test extension (`addon/utils.ts`), where it finds the registrable domain for the per-site on/off switch. esbuild bundles it into the extension at build time.

title: Add Turkish heuristic patterns
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

The heuristic does not read Turkish cookie notices yet. `DETECT_PATTERNS` has no Turkish entry, so the heuristic never acts on a Turkish banner that no rule covers, even though `REJECT_PATTERNS_TURKISH` already has `reddet`. This PR adds Turkish support:

- **Detect patterns.**
  - Turkish puts the verb last, so the main pattern allows a gap of up to 200 characters within one sentence. The gap runs from the cookie word (`çerez`, `cookie`, `tanımlama bilgi…`) to a present-tense "use" verb (`kullanıyoruz`, `kullanmaktayız`, `kullanılmakta`, `kullanılır`, `yararlanıyoruz`, …).
  - The verb endings keep out `Çerez Politikası ve Kullanım Koşulları` links and the other meaning of `çerez` (snacks).
  - Two smaller patterns cover `kullandığımız çerezler` and `Çerez Politikamızı inceleyebilirsiniz`.
- **Reject buttons.** `tümünü / hepsini / tüm çerezleri / çerezleri / isteğe bağlı çerezleri / zorunlu olmayan çerezleri reddet`, `reddet ve kapat`, `reddediyorum`, `kabul etmiyorum`. The existing `reddet` and `çerezleri reddet` are covered by the new regex.
- **Settings buttons.** `çerez ayarları`, `tanımlama bilgisi ayarları`, `ayarlar`, `tercihler`, `seçenekler`, `çerezleri / tercihleri yönet`, `çerez tercihlerini yapılandır`, `kişiselleştir`. With these, a Turkish banner that offers settings next to "Kabul Et" is not treated as accept-only.
- **Text in capitals** (defacto.com.tr shows its banner that way):
  - The `i` flag pairs neither `ı` with `I` nor `i` with `İ`, so the detect patterns use `[ıI]` and `[iİ]`.
  - `toLowerCase()` maps `I` to `i`, so the button patterns accept `i` where Turkish has `ı`.
  - `toLowerCase()` turns `İ` into `i` plus a combining dot above, so `cleanButtonText` now drops U+0307.

I checked the patch on live pages from Turkey on 2026-10-24. I bundled `getActionablePopups('reject')` from this branch and ran it read-only (no clicks) in a fresh Firefox profile. It found the banner and classified its reject button as `reject` on these sites:

- mediamarkt.com.tr, lcw.com, defacto.com.tr and getir.com, which no rule covers today, and vatanbilgisayar.com.
- trendyol.com and hurriyet.com.tr: OneTrust.
- turkcell.com.tr, flo.com.tr and haberturk.com: the button is inside a shadow root.

The test texts come from those banners, plus hepsiburada.com, migros.com.tr, boyner.com.tr and carrefoursa.com.

Suggested labels: `version: patch`, `category: enhancement`.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. Run `npm run test:lib`. The new cases are:
   - `tests-wtr/heuristics/heuristics-utils.test.ts`: Turkish detection, Turkish reject and settings buttons (including capitals), and `cleanButtonText` with `İ`.
   - `tests-wtr/heuristics/get-actionable-popups.*`: a Turkish popup with "Reddet" is actionable, one with "Kabul Et" and "Çerez Ayarları" is not tier2, and a snack offer that says "çerez" is ignored.
2. Run `npm run benchmark-buttons`. The numbers should not change, which means no new false positives on `data/labelled-button-texts.csv`.
3. Run `npm run lint`.

I could not run the proxy-based regional checks, so every site above was checked from Turkey only.

## Description:

Adds Greek (EL) patterns to the heuristic, which had no Greek coverage before:

- **Detect:** "χρησιμοποιούμε / χρησιμοποιεί cookies", "cookies και άλλες παρόμοιες τεχνολογίες", consent + cookies, "αποδοχή όλων", "απόρριψη όλων".
- **Reject:** "απόρριψη" / "απορρίπτω", "άρνηση", only-necessary/mandatory ("αποδοχή υποχρεωτικών", "μόνο τα απαραίτητα cookies"), "συνέχεια χωρίς αποδοχή", "δεν / δε αποδέχομαι / συμφωνώ", "όχι, ευχαριστώ".
- **Settings:** "ρυθμίσεις", "πληροφορίες και ρυθμίσεις", "διαχείριση cookies", "προσαρμογή", "περισσότερες επιλογές". Without these, an Accept + Settings popup was classified as tier2.
- **Accept:** "αποδοχή (όλων)", "αποδέχομαι", "συμφωνώ", "(να) επιτρέπονται όλα", "επιτρέπεται η επιλογή".
- **Acknowledge:** "εντάξει", "(το) κατάλαβα", "κλείσιμο", "συνέχεια", "αποθήκευση επιλογών".

Vowels are matched with and without tonos, because all-caps Greek buttons drop it ("ΑΠΟΔΟΧΗ ΟΛΩΝ" lowercases to "αποδοχη ολων"). `\w` and `\b` do not match Greek letters, so the patterns use `\s` / `\S` and anchors instead.

Results:
- **Button benchmark:** 0 false positives. All 10 Greek rows already in `labelled-button-texts.csv` now classify correctly; all were missed before. Overall accuracy goes from 96.2% to 96.3%.
- **Live tests:** done through a residential proxy from GR, with the heuristic in tier2 mode.

| Site | gr | us | gb | de |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| e-shop.gr | HEURISTIC-REJECT ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| efood.gr | HEURISTIC-REJECT ✅ | Cloudflare bot wall | Cloudflare bot wall | ✅ |

After opt-out, a reload no longer matches. Screenshots confirm the banners are gone.

Negative checks: "Απόρρητο" (privacy), "Πολιτική cookies", "Πολιτική απορρήτου", and the skai.gr push-notification prompt ("ΟΧΙ, ΕΥΧΑΡΙΣΤΩ / ΝΑΙ, ΘΕΛΩ") are not matched.

Limitation: only 2 live Greek popups were found. Most of the 36 Greek sites surveyed either use CMPs that rules already handle (Quantcast, OneTrust, Cookiebot), or showed no consent UI to the headless test browser.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run test:lib`: the new Greek cases are in `tests-wtr/heuristics/heuristics-utils.test.ts`.
2. `npm run benchmark-buttons`: there should be 0 false positives.
3. Optional: load https://www.e-shop.gr/ or https://www.efood.gr/ from an EU IP with `heuristicMode: 'reject'` and confirm the reject button is clicked.

title: Update stale rules: replace generated rules with hand-maintained rules
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1220293578510493

## Description:

Stacked on duckduckgo/autoconsent#2544. This is the update step of the same regression sweep. Rules whose sites still show a consent popup the rule no longer handles are fixed. Stale generated rules are replaced with hand-maintained rules in `rules/autoconsent/`. Where the popup comes from a shared CMP, the replacement is one generic rule. This PR changes no generated rule in place.

**How it was tested:**
- Every new or changed rule was tested in US, GB and DE, plus the regions of the rules it replaces.
- Each generic rule was tested on at least two sites and got a mobile check.
- Every final screenshot was reviewed. Pages were reloaded to confirm the rule no longer matches.
- A rule was only removed when, with the rule taken out, another rule or the heuristic handled the site, or the site showed no consent popup.
- Every site whose rule this stack removes because the heuristic handled it (101 sites) was rechecked against current main. See "Sites the heuristic no longer handles" below.
- The changed shared rules were run on every known site in US, GB, DE, FR, NL, PL, AU, CA and JP: `axeptio` on 13 sites, `Uniconsent` on 7 and `pandectes` on 12. Where `axeptio` or `Uniconsent` still fail, the current rules on main fail the same way (see "Known issues").

### New generic rules

| Rule | CMP | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| `atruvia-consent-layer` | `hra-consent-layer-ui` dialog on cooperative bank sites | 8 generated rules |
| `trustcommander` | Commanders Act TrustCommander | 11 generated rules (laposte, labanquepostale, axa.de, 3ds, maty, …) |
| `outdooractive` | outdooractive maps | 6 generated rules |
| `niceshops` | niceshops stores | 5 generated rules (3djake, ecco-verde, vitalabo) |
| `jtl-consent-manager` | JTL shop consent manager | 4 generated rules |
| `sg-cookie-optin` | SgCookieOptin (TYPO3) | 2 generated rules |
| `bzga-matomo` | Matomo banner on federal health sites | 2 generated rules |
| `whitecube-cookie-consent` | whitecube/laravel-cookie-consent | onestream.co.uk; spec also covers ddw.nl and woomie.ro |
| `focal-cookie-bar` | Shopify Focal theme cookie bar | hacksmith.store; spec also covers zuckersuessverlag.de and obumi.de |
| `kixell` | Kixell | magellan-bio.fr; spec also covers ocarat.com and mamaisonmonjardin.com |
| `statamic-peak` | Statamic Peak consent banner | beducated.com; spec also covers gehaltsreporter.de, 10design.co and cath.ch |
| `cmsbox` | Cmsbox cookie warning | gstaadmenuhinfestival.ch; spec also covers vivanta.ch and abenco.ch |
| `carlsberg-group` | Carlsberg Group compliance pack | feldschloesschen.ch (removed in #2492); spec also covers carlsberggroup.com, kronenbourg.com and teisseire.fr |
| `ancestry` | Ancestry's banner across its domains | ancestry.com (removed in #2492); spec also covers ancestry.co.uk and ancestry.de |
| `magefan` | Magefan Cookie Consent (Magento) | meinduft.de (left unhandled in #2544); spec also covers tileexperience.co.uk and silencershop.com |

How some of them work:
- **`trustcommander`:** its sites use different templates, so the refuse button's position and label change from site to site. The rule calls TrustCommander's own `tC.privacy.clickBanner('optout')` through new eval snippets. Sites that hide the TrustCommander banner and show their own dialog (sparkasse.de, lbs.de) are left to the heuristic, which rejects there.
- **`whitecube-cookie-consent`:** clicks "Only essentials" when the banner has it. Otherwise it opens Customize, unticks the optional categories and saves.
- **`statamic-peak`:** clicks Reject all, opening Manage preferences first if needed. Where a site has no Reject button (cath.ch), it unticks the optional categories and saves.
- **`focal-cookie-bar`:** the theme removes the bar's `hidden` attribute late on some loads, so the rule only detects a bar that is showing.

### New site rules

| Rule | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `fca-cookielaw` (consent iframe) | 4 Stellantis/FCA rules (alfaromeo.de, fiat.de, jeep.de, fiat.fr) |
| `dropbox` (consent iframe) | 2 help.dropbox.com duplicates |
| `truecaller` (consent iframe) | 3 truecaller rules |
| `bayern-matomo` | 3 Bavarian government rules |
| `flinders-edu-au`, `spankbang` | 3 rules each |
| `yandex` | translate.yandex.com |
| `bestsecret`, `charliehebdo`, `edumoov`, `effenaar`, `fondationbeyeler`, `greengo`, `kathmandu-nl`, `lethpolytech`, `livejasmin`, `mypharmacy.co.uk` | one generated rule each |
| `aoc.com`, `stoneacre.co.uk`, `fawesome.tv` | rules removed in #2492 (see below) |
| `ihk-muenchen.de` | nothing; the site's own banner was left unhandled in #2544 |

`fca-cookielaw`, `dropbox` and `truecaller` run inside the consent iframe. They wait for the page to show the frame (`EVAL_IFRAME_SHOWN`) before clicking. lethpolytech's Decline button only reacts to `mouseup`, so its rule uses an eval snippet.

In total, this PR replaces 72 generated rules. It also brings back handling for 5 sites whose generated rules #2492 removes. And it covers 4 of the 5 spec sites that #2544 lists as unhandled: voba-rhein-erft-koeln.de (`atruvia-consent-layer`), aeris.de (`pandectes`), meinduft.de (`magefan`) and ihk-muenchen.de. The fifth, dedeman.ro, is covered by duckduckgo/autoconsent#2669.

### Sites the heuristic no longer handles

After the recent detect-pattern changes on main (#2593 and others), the heuristic no longer handles 5 sites whose rules #2492 removes. This PR adds hand-maintained rules for them:
- feldschloesschen.ch: `carlsberg-group`
- ancestry.com: `ancestry`
- aoc.com
- stoneacre.co.uk
- fawesome.tv

Of the other 96 rechecked sites:
- 84 still get a heuristic opt-out.
- 6 are now handled by other rules.
- 3 show no popup.
- 2 couldn't be reached.
- denniskirk.com now offers only Accept, so it gets no rule.

### Fixed rules

- **Hand-maintained:**
  - `Uniconsent`: the popup now sits inside a shadow root.
  - `pabcogypsum`: new Privacy Settings dialog.
  - `rt`: rt.com now redirects to rt-english.com.
  - `axeptio`: new widget layout on savelys.fr.
  - `pandectes`: finds the banner by its classes, because some shops rename `#pandectes-banner` (aeris.de).
  - `ct-ultimate-gdpr`: second settings-modal layout.
  - `ionos.de`: now also covers ionos.co.uk and ionos.fr.
  - `strato.de`, `lendable` and `zentralruf-de`.
- **Spec sites refreshed:** `EU Cookie Law`, `UK Cookie Consent`, `blocksy`, `tccCmpAlert` and `ccm19`. tccCmpAlert's popup now shows first only in the US.
- **`msn` spec:** `'UK'` is changed to `'GB'`, because the runner never matched `UK`.

### Removed rules (29)

| Why | Rules | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Another rule handles the site | ccm19 (8), consentmo (sprinklr, fr.xgimi.com), ionos.de (ionos.co.uk), OneTrust (`cookiealert`; Kaufland moved to OneTrust, and referencement-manuel.com is a Cookiebot dialog that the Cookiebot rule handles) | 12 |
| The heuristic rejects | rundfunkbeitrag, denieuwebibliotheek, goteborg, saseurobonusmastercard, sparkasse, lbs, biunsinnorden, livegigs | 8 |
| No consent popup anymore | lilly, `financestrategists.com`, 6 Yandex sites | 8 |
| Site gone | howik.com | 1 |

### Left unchanged because they couldn't be tested

- **kobo.com:** during testing the site's scripts and styles didn't load, so the banner buttons never enabled.
- **bobvoyeur:** the age gate leads to a real ID check.
- **pichunter:** the site redirected to google.com.
- **bestsecret android and orders subdomains:** they return 403.
- **9 Yandex rules on .ru and .by domains:** these sites couldn't be reached.
- **7 TrustCommander rules** (mrporter, net-a-porter, two Sephora sites, gmf, norauto, pointp): these sites block automated visits.
- **truecar and bswhealth.**

### Known issues

- **`fca-cookielaw` (2 of about 12 runs):** FCA sites redirect to `?adobe_mc_ref=` right after the first load. The click sometimes lands on the page that is about to navigate away, so the banner stays until the next load, which handles it. The old generated rules did the same. The spec uses the `?adobe_mc_ref=` URLs.
- **`fawesome.tv`:** the banner's only choices are Accept All and a Manage link that leaves the page. The rule clicks the close button, which hides the banner without consenting. The site stores nothing in that case, so the banner returns, and is closed again, on every visit. The page doesn't reload.
- **`focal-cookie-bar`:** on one load out of several, the heuristic acted before the bar finished appearing. It rejected, so the popup was still handled.
- **`UK Cookie Consent` sites in GB and DE:** a separate Google Funding Choices dialog stays open after the cosmetic rule runs. The old spec sites behaved the same way.
- **aeris.de (`pandectes`):** on slow loads the banner appears up to about 20 seconds after page load, after detection has stopped, so its spec may be flaky.
- **silencershop.com (`magefan`):** the shop hides the decline button. The rule still clicks it, and the site records a refusal.
- **Existing gaps this PR doesn't change:** `axeptio` fails on can-am.brp.com in AU and CA, where the widget has no reject button, only a "Continue without consent" tab. It also misses widgets that appear late (welcometothejungle.com and lemlist.com outside Europe). `Uniconsent` fails on offen.net's French variant (FR, NL, PL) and misses tvarticles.org in AU and JP. The current rules on main behave the same way on all of these.
- **Self-tests:** these sometimes fail even when the screenshot shows the popup handled:
  - `ct-ultimate-gdpr`.
  - Pages that reload after the click: `pabcogypsum`, `bzga-matomo` and `outdooractive` on mobile. `cmsbox` also reloads after the click, so its spec turns the self-test off.
  - `m.livejasmin` on mobile.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish && npm run lint` should pass.
2. `npm run test:lib` should pass.
3. CI E2E: the new and changed specs should pass in their regions. The deleted generated specs no longer run.

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Fixes blocked scrolling on Mondadori network sites (nostrofiglio.it, soldionline.it, pianetamamma.it, valorinormali.com, giallozafferano.it and others) that use a custom iubenda banner template (`#ameConsentUI`). Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220591299002629?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific rule for the custom cookie banner on La Tinka (latinka.com.pe), a Peruvian lottery site. The banner only offers "Configurar cookies" and "Aceptar todas", and the "Rechazar todas" button lives in a second-layer settings modal, so the heuristic flow does not handle it. The rule clicks the site's own reject button (#rejectCustomizationsBtn) without opening the modal, which avoids leaving a Bootstrap backdrop or scroll lock behind. It then waits for the banner to hide. The self-test checks the ad_storage=denied cookie.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `REGION=AU npx playwright test tests/latinka.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 1 --retries 1`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Rule update: boxprivacy
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220591509976888?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Unsupported common CMP

Adds a generic `boxprivacy` rule for a notice-only cookie banner (`#boxprivacy`) that many sites share through a common site template. The banner has Indonesian text ("Kami menggunakan cookies…") and a single × dismiss control (`.closebox`), and it offers no accept or reject choice. The heuristic does not handle it: none of its detect patterns covers this Indonesian wording, and the × is a plain div rather than a button-like element. The rule detects `#boxprivacy .closebox`, treats the popup as open when `#boxprivacy` is visible, clicks the × to dismiss it for both opt-out and opt-in, and checks that the banner is no longer visible. The spec covers four sites, including both the dark and light theme variants.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/boxprivacy.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 2`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Rule update: nfl
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220539240182683?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Adds an `nfl` rule for NFL league pages (nfl.com) and the 32 NFL club sites, all of which share the same platform (`body.nfl-is-league-site` / `body.nfl-is-club-site`) and use OneTrust. On these pages an inline script reloads the page synchronously when a OneTrust banner button is clicked. OneTrust saves consent in a deferred `setTimeout`, and in the US its reject path first runs an async global opt-out step. The reload often wins that race, so the reject is never saved and the banner comes back on every load, which causes a reload loop with autoconsent. The new rule detects the OneTrust banner only on these platform pages and calls `OneTrust.RejectAll()` / `OneTrust.AllowAll()` through new eval snippets instead of clicking. It then waits for the banner to hide. Consent is saved reliably and no reload happens. Clients that receive the rule without the new snippets fall back to clicking the banner button, which matches what the generic OneTrust rule does today. The fallback is skipped when the banner closes on its own within 5 seconds, because a timed-out eval may still have run the API call. nfl.com's Next.js pages (homepage, news, schedules) do not have the inline reload script and still use the generic OneTrust rule.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/nfl.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 3 --retries 1`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Onetrust: dismiss notice-only banners with an icon Close button
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1216652646972579

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

The OneTrust code rule already dismisses notice-only banners, where Close is the only control and there is no Accept, Reject or Settings, but it only recognises them by the `ot-close-btn-link` class on `#onetrust-banner-sdk`. Some notice-only banners use an icon Close button and don't have that class. On those, opt-out fell through to the "show settings" path, which has nothing to click. The rule still reported success, but the banner stayed on screen.

This change detects a notice-only banner by a `.onetrust-close-btn-handler` inside the banner, plus the existing check that no Accept/Reject/Preferences/"show settings" control exists on the page. It only changes the outcome for banners that had no working opt-out path before; any banner with a Reject or Preferences control still goes the same way as today.

Adds bestbuy.ca to the OneTrust spec as an example of the icon-Close variant.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/onetrust.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 4 --retries 1`, with `REGION`/`PROXY_SERVER` set per region.
- Without this change the bestbuy.ca spec test also passes, but its final screenshot still shows the banner. Check the screenshot, not just the test result.

Local validation:
- `npm run lint` and `npm run test:lib` pass.
- bestbuy.ca, through regional proxies in all 15 supported regions on desktop and mobile (Pixel 7): opt-out succeeded and the banner is gone in every screenshot; after a reload the popup is not detected again.
- Full OneTrust spec in US, GB, DE and CA, compared against the base commit: no new failures. The failures that remain also occur on the base commit (sites that show no OneTrust banner in that region, self-test results not arriving).

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

title: Rule update: t-cookie-bar
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220655187197052?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a generic `t-cookie-bar` rule for a custom cookie notice bar ("This website uses cookies to ensure you get the best experience on our website." with a "Got it!" control rendered as `div.t-cookie-bar`). The same bar appears on a family of sibling game and AI-directory sites (peppalearning.com, gamemasha.com, lukogames.com, meta00s.com, metakidsplay.com, meta1s.com, 4kzgame.com, paintbyclick.com, theabclearning.com, besttoolforai.com, betteraitool.com). The control is a plain div, so the heuristic button search misses it. The bar is a notice with no reject option, so the rule clicks its acknowledge control. In GDPR regions these sites load a Google Funding Choices dialog about 2s after the bar. Once this rule has taken the page, the separate funding-choices rule would no longer run, so the rule's opt-out waits briefly for that dialog and rejects it. This follows the pattern of existing rules such as silver-nu and b1ng-cc.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/t-cookie-bar.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 3`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Rule update: sarmady
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220637472373690?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a `sarmady` rule for the custom Arabic cookie consent banner shared by FilGoal (`#fg-consent-banner`) and FilFan (`#ff-consent-banner`). Neither the existing rules nor the heuristic detected it, because the heuristic has no Arabic patterns. The banner has four consent toggles plus Accept ("قبول") and Close ("إغلاق") buttons. Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220655185634093?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Unsupported common CMP

Adds a generic `smartstore` rule for the built-in cookie manager of the Smartstore e-commerce platform (`#cookie-manager-window` modal, `Smartstore.Cmp`). Before this change the heuristic reported success but only clicked the 'Notwendige Cookies' accordion header, so the dialog stayed open. Smartstore also sets a default consent cookie with analytics allowed, so the visitor was left opted in. The rule unchecks any enabled optional categories and submits the selection with 'Auswahl bestätigen' (save selection), then waits for the modal to close. The self-test checks that the `.Smart.CookieConsent` cookie stores `AllowAnalytics:false`. The spec covers greatbritishfood.de, farben-hornauer.de and smartstore.com in DE.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `PROXY_SERVER=$REGIONAL_PROXY_DE REGION=DE npx playwright test tests/smartstore.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 2 --retries 1`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1219678736349153?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific rule for the cookie notice on bom.gov.au (Bureau of Meteorology). The banner says "We use cookies on our site – see our privacy policy for details" and has one "Ok" acknowledge button. It is part of the site's own design system, not a shared CMP. It sits in the normal page flow rather than being fixed or positioned, so the heuristic DOM walk does not find it. The rule finds the alert by its link to /privacy inside the site's alerts container and clicks the acknowledge button, which is the only control. The self-test waits for the banner to disappear.

title: Regional testing harness: disabledCmps, heuristicMode, gpc and device emulation
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1217862416204870
Tech Design: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/72649045549333/task/1217862323216728?focus=true

## Description:

New options for the regional testing harness behind the `proxy-testing` and `oxylabs-testing` skills:

- `disabledCmps`: rules autoconsent skips, to see what handles a page without them.
- `heuristicMode`: the heuristic level. `'tier1'` leaves out popups whose only button is Accept.
- `emulateDevice`: a Playwright device for Chromium, such as `'Pixel 7'` (viewport, user agent, touch). Prefer Android: an emulated iPhone on Chromium still exposes `navigator.userAgentData`.
- `gpc`: send the Global Privacy Control signal (`Sec-GPC: 1` and `navigator.globalPrivacyControl`), as DuckDuckGo browsers do. On by default; `gpc: false` tests the way a spec without the `gpc` option does.

The other defaults are unchanged.

On Oxylabs, `device: 'mobile'` now opens the page with touch and a 360×740 viewport, keeping Oxylabs' Android user agent. Before, it got a 1280px desktop page with no touch. Pages still stay at least 500px wide, and `navigator.userAgentData` still reports desktop Linux.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish`, then `node --test .agents/skills/proxy-testing/scripts/regional-proxy.test.mjs .agents/skills/oxylabs-testing/scripts/oxylabs.test.mjs` (20 passing).
2. Regional proxy: `testUrl('https://www.spiegel.de/', 'de', { emulateDevice: 'Pixel 7', heuristicMode: 'tier1' })` passes with a mobile screenshot. Adding the rule that acted to `disabledCmps` changes the outcome.
3. Oxylabs: `testUrl('https://de.ccm.net/', 'de', { device: 'mobile' })` gets the mobile layout in a 360×740 screenshot.
4. Oxylabs, with GPC on: 411.com and whitepages.com in the US are handled by `whitepages-gpc-banner`.
5. `npx prettier --check .agents` passes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add SearchWebCode search skill as a PublicWWW fallback
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1201844467387842/task/1220652902757537

## Description:

Adds a `searchwebcode-search` agent skill that searches website source code through the [SearchWebCode](https://www.searchwebcode.com/docs) API. It serves the same purpose as `publicwww-search` (is a popup from a shared CMP, more test sites for a rule, how widespread a banner pattern is), but agents use it only as a fallback once PublicWWW's daily limit is used up.

- `.agents/skills/searchwebcode-search/SKILL.md` (+ `.claude/skills/` stub): when to fall back, API and query syntax, cost (free `counts_only` first, stop on 402/429), and examples that print PublicWWW-style `url;rank;snippet` lines. It notes that SearchWebCode indexes homepage HTML only (no JS/CSS files).
- `AGENTS.md`: a fallback paragraph under "CMP Discovery with PublicWWW", and the cross-site prevalence and spec-URL guidance name the fallback.
- `publicwww-search` skill (all three copies): says how to recognise the daily limit and to switch.
- `.claude/user-settings.json.TEMPLATE`: adds `SEARCHWEBCODE_KEY`.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. Set `SEARCHWEBCODE_KEY` and run one of the skill's examples, e.g. the `counts_only` query for `"sd-cmp"`. Check it returns JSON with `total`.
2. Ask an agent in this repo to check a CMP's prevalence, telling it PublicWWW answered with a daily-limit message. Check that it switches to `searchwebcode-search`.
3. `npx prettier --check AGENTS.md .agents .claude .cursor`

title: Rule update: Rule fix for Site Breakage: Layout broken on drive-clean-air-zone.service.gov.uk
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1210200952101023?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Fixes false-positive popup detection in the generic `gov.uk` rule (GOV.UK Design System cookie banner). Many GOV.UK services keep the dismissed cookie banner in the DOM and hide it after consent is stored, for example with `display: none` or the `hidden` attribute. The rule's `detectPopup` used `exists` on `.govuk-cookie-banner__message .govuk-button`, so it matched on every page load after consent. It then ran an opt-out that always failed, because there was nothing to click. This was seen on drive-clean-air-zone.service.gov.uk, www.gov.uk, data.gov.uk, find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk and ewf.companieshouse.gov.uk. `detectPopup` now requires at least one banner button to be visible (`visible` with `check: "any"`). That still covers the initial accept/reject state and the server-rendered "Hide this message" confirmation.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `PROXY_SERVER=$REGIONAL_PROXY_GB REGION=GB npx playwright test tests/gov-uk.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 2`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220689391230723?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific rule for the custom cookie banner on funpay.com. The banner has only "Accept all" and "Customize" buttons. The rule opts out by opening the Customize dialog, unticking the analytics/third-party option if it is ticked (it is off by default), and clicking Save. That stores `cookie_prefs=0`, which the self-test checks. Opt-in clicks "Accept all". The banner appears in UK/EEA/CA/AU but not in the US or JP, so the spec skips US and JP.

title: Rule update: samsung-account
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220689391312698?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a site-specific `samsung-account` rule for the cookie notice on Samsung Account (account.samsung.com / v3.account.samsung.com). The notice is a bottom drawer ("About our cookies – Our site uses essential cookies only") with a dimming backdrop and a scroll lock. It has no accept or reject choice, only an icon close button, so the text-based heuristic cannot act on it. The rule finds the drawer that links to the cookie policy and clicks its close button (`data-log-id="close"`). This removes the backdrop and the scroll lock, and the site stores `sa_enable=on`, which the rule's self-test checks. The notice appears in European regions but not in the US, so the spec skips US.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `PROXY_SERVER=$REGIONAL_PROXY_GB REGION=GB npx playwright test tests/samsung-account.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 1 --retries 1`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

title: Harden unit test browser launch in CI
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

The `test` job in the Validate workflow fails intermittently before any unit test runs. Web Test Runner's default launcher drives the runner image's system Chrome (`/usr/bin/google-chrome-stable`) with a 30s start timeout, and on a cold runner Chrome sometimes takes longer than that to start:

- When Chrome never comes up within 30s, all 38 test files fail with `Timed out after 30000 ms while waiting for the WS endpoint URL to appear in stdout!` ([example run](https://github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent/actions/runs/44496979888/job/135466590444)). The same commit passed on its push run moments earlier.
- When Chrome comes up just after 30s, the first test files fail with `The browser was unable to create and start a test page after 30000ms` and the rest pass. The run still exits 1 with only `Error while running tests` and "754 passed, 0 failed" ([example run](https://github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent/actions/runs/44454219078)).

Changes:
- `web-test-runner.config.mjs`: use `@web/test-runner-playwright` (already a devDependency, previously unused) so tests run in Playwright's Chromium headless shell. It is lighter to start than full Chrome and pinned by our lockfile, so runner image updates can't change it.
- Raise `browserStartTimeout`, `testsStartTimeout` and the browser launch timeout from 30s to 120s. A slow start then makes the run slower instead of failing it.
- `.github/workflows/checks.yml`: install the headless shell (`npx playwright install --only-shell chromium`) before `npm run test:lib`.

Running `npm run test:lib` locally now requires Playwright's Chromium, which anyone running the E2E tests already has via `npx playwright install`.

Labels: `version: patch`, `category: tests`

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npx playwright install --only-shell chromium`
2. `npm run build-rules && npm run test:lib`, and check that all test files pass (766 tests passed locally in ~16s)
3. Check that the Validate / `test` job passes on this PR

title: Add CookieOfficer rule
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

This PR adds a generic JSON rule for CookieOfficer, a consent management platform (CMP) developed by DataWolves (Poland).

- Website: https://cookieofficer.com
- Script host: `cdn.cookieofficer.com` (`/s/co-<site id>.js`)
- Files:
  - `rules/autoconsent/cookieofficer.json`
  - `tests/cookieofficer.spec.ts`

A JSON rule is enough here, so there is no code-based rule.

The banner is rendered in an open shadow root on `div[data-co-banner]`, so all selectors are arrays that start from that host. They use fixed attributes and classes from the CookieOfficer script, the same on every site and in every language:
- `.co-btns button[data-co-action='accept' | 'reject' | 'manage']`
- `.co-switch`

`optOut` covers the two layouts seen on real sites:
1. If the first layer has a "Reject" button, it clicks it.
2. If there is no "Reject" button, it clicks "Customize", waits for the category switches and clicks "Save". Optional categories are off by default (opt-in), so this saves the necessary category only. If the switches are already shown on the first layer, it clicks "Save" directly.

If a site owner sets the banner to a single "Accept" button, `optOut` fails instead of accepting (no TIER2 click).

Consent is stored in the first-party `co_consent` cookie (URL-encoded JSON). The self-test checks that the cookie exists and that `analytics`, `marketing` and `personalization` are not `true`.

The spec covers both layouts:
- with "Reject": https://demo.cookieofficer.com/, https://placowkijutra.pl/, https://pipelinedesigner.pl/
- without "Reject": https://smartanimal.pl/, https://growthmeetup.com/, https://adsetterka.pl/

Other sites confirmed to load the script from cdn.cookieofficer.com:
- https://cialoczulosc.studio
- https://kateaugustyniak.pl
- https://uratuj.com
- https://kurs.uratuj.com
- https://kursysos.pl
- https://cambridge-diagnostics.pl
- https://google.ed-era.com/ai-for-business/
- https://datawolves.pl
- https://cookieofficer.pl
- https://ga4audit.io

Suggested labels: `category: rules`, `version: minor`.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish`
2. `npx playwright test tests/cookieofficer.spec.ts --project chrome`
3. `npx playwright test tests/cookieofficer.spec.ts --project webkit`

Results, run from Poland without a proxy:
- Chrome: 12/12 passed. optIn, optOut and the self-test passed on all 6 sites.
- WebKit: 12/12 passed.
- `npm run lint` passes. It includes Prettier and `rule-syntax-check`.
- After opt-out and a reload, the banner host is no longer in the page, so the rule does not match again.

Not run: the US, GB and DE proxy checks, and the mobile project.

Tested on https://demo.cookieofficer.com.

title: Rule update: amazon.com
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

Opt-out on Amazon stores was slow: the `amazon.com` rule waited an unconditional 5 seconds between the banner becoming visible and clicking Reject (same for Accept). The wait was added a while ago because early clicks were being dropped.

The Reject button is now a plain form submit, so an early click is handled. This replaces the fixed wait with `waitForThenClick` plus `retry: 5` / `retryInterval: 1000`: the click lands as soon as the button is visible, and is repeated only if the banner is still showing.

Time from popup detection to the opt-out click went from ~5,000 ms to 9–64 ms.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish`
2. Open an Amazon EU store (e.g. amazon.nl, amazon.de, amazon.co.uk) with the extension and check that the banner is rejected right away and does not come back after a reload.

Tested in US, GB, DE and NL on amazon.co.uk, .de, .nl, .fr, .it, .es, .se, .pl and .com.be (desktop), plus mobile on amazon.nl and opt-in on .de and .co.uk. Every load that showed the banner was opted out, with no banner after reload; screenshots checked.

Notes:
- Amazon decides per session whether to show the banner at all, so some loads show no banner in any region.
- amazon.com did not show a consent banner in any region tested; the rule correctly does not fire there.
- Without a regional IP, Amazon may show a "continue shopping" bot check before the page loads, which makes the E2E spec report "no CMP detected" regardless of this change.

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

MercadoLibre, Mercado Livre and MercadoPago show the same cookie banner on non-www subdomains (e.g. `vendedores.*` and `developers.*`). There, "Configurar cookies" opens a modal that embeds `www.<domain>/privacy-preferences/cookies?mode=embed`. - **`mercadolibre-frame`** (new, frame only): runs inside the embedded preferences page, and only when its parent is cross-origin. It waits for the toggles to hydrate (they are server-rendered as disabled), switches off every optional category, and posts the page's own `saveCookiesPreference` message, the same one the parent's Save button sends. The iframe then saves the choices and tells the parent to close the modal.

Two eval snippets are added for this (`EVAL_MERCADOLIBRE_CROSS_ORIGIN_PARENT`, `EVAL_MERCADOLIBRE_SAVE`), so clients need a release before the frame rule can run; until then they behave as today.

The spec covers vendedores.mercadolibre.com.ar, vendedores.mercadolivre.com.br, vendedores.mercadolibre.com.mx, developers.mercadolibre.com.ar and developers.mercadolibre.com.mx. On www sites only `mercadolibre` matches, as before.

title: Only count the PR's own files as modified in Jenkins PR builds
body:
In a PR build, `HEAD` is the merge commit Jenkins made against the target branch as it was at checkout. `getModifiedFiles()` diffed `origin/main` against `HEAD` (two-dot). When `main` moves on before the Test stage runs, for example when many PRs merge in a short time, that diff also lists every file merged to `main` in between. `scripts/get-tests-to-run.js` then runs specs for unrelated rules, and `Tests / Changed files` can fail on sites the PR never touched.

This diffs against the merge base (`origin/main...HEAD`), so only the PR's own changes count. The result is the same as before when `main` hasn't moved.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Run fewer tests per Jenkins PR build
body:
PR builds run every changed spec in all 9 CI regions, for both optIn and optOut. This change cuts that down:

- **No optIn tests in CI** (`SKIP_OPT_IN=1`). Specs that only test optIn fall back to a detection-only `noaction` test.
- **At most 3 regions per spec** (`CI_REGIONS`). A spec runs in US, then its `onlyRegions` in the order written, then regions picked with the PR number as the seed (`CI_SEED`) until there are 3. `skipRegions` still applies. The seed keeps a PR on the same regions across builds, while different PRs spread over all 9.

Listing the full suite drops from ~67.5k to ~12.5k tests across the 9 regions. Running tests locally works as before unless these variables are set.

title: sicredi: run the generic rule in the top frame only
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220591298972132

## Description:

The generic `sicredi` rule (added in #2697) has `runContext: { main: true, frame: true }` and no `urlPattern`. That makes it the only JSON rule that matches every subframe, so its `detectCmp` runs in every iframe (ads, embeds) on every site.

Frame support is only needed on the Sicredi internet banking login pages, `ibpj.sicredi.com.br` and `ibpf.sicredi.com.br`. Both are framesets whose single same-origin `<frame>` (`/ib-view/…`) renders the banner. On the other Sicredi sites the banner is in the top document.

This PR splits the rule:

- `sicredi`: generic, top frame only (default `runContext`).
- `sicredi-frame` (new): subframes only, limited to `sicredi.com.br` frames by `urlPattern`. Same steps as `sicredi`.

With per-frame compact rule filtering, an unrelated iframe now gets no `sicredi*` rule; the banking frames get `sicredi-frame` only.

**Why not reach the frame from the top frame with array selectors** (`["frame", "#sicredi-cookies-root"]`)? It works, but only when the frame renders the banner quickly. A frameset document does not change after load, and after its first detection attempts `findCmp` waits for a mutation of the top document before trying again. With the `/ib-view/` request delayed by 4s, a top-frame-only rule never detected the banner, while the rule running inside the frame did.

**Testing** (opt-out, then reload; screenshots checked):

| Site | Rule | US | GB | DE | BR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ibpj.sicredi.com.br | `sicredi-frame` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ desktop and mobile |
| ibpf.sicredi.com.br | `sicredi-frame` | ✅ | Access Denied | Access Denied | ✅ |
| auniaofazavida.com.br | `sicredi` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ desktop and mobile |
| www.sicredi.com.br | `sicredi` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (2nd load) | ✅ |

- After reload, every site reports `cmpDetected` without `popupFound`, and opt-out does not run again.
- Akamai shows "Access Denied" on most Sicredi hosts to the test browsers, so those runs used `OXYLABS=1`. On ibpf this also happens from GB and DE, so its spec entry runs in US only; ibpj covers the same frameset in every region.
- www.sicredi.com.br sometimes renders the cookie container without the banner on a load ("expected popup not found"). Run alone 3 times, its US opt-out test passed 3/3 with the rule from `main` and 3/3 with this branch.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npm run build-rules`
- `OXYLABS=1 REGION=US npx playwright test tests/sicredi.spec.ts tests/sicredi-frame.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 2`

title: Rule sweep 2026-11-23: remove 3, fix 1, update specs of 5 rules
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220808449910050?focus=true

## Description:

Automated regression sweep of autoconsent rules, their spec sites and top sites.

Rule sweep for 2026-11-23: 27 rules and 9 top sites tested.

**Spec updates.** amex and twcc: americanexpress.com and wise.com no longer show a consent popup in the US, so those specs now skip the US. civic-cookie-control: removed planning.org.uk, which now uses Google Funding Choices, and birmingham.gov.uk, which answers automated test browsers with 403 Forbidden in most runs. craft-cookie-consent: removed telephonics.com, which switched to Klaro. WP Cookie Notice for GDPR: removed meyer-koering.de, which no longer shows a popup. Yahoo: www.yahoo.com no longer redirects to the Yahoo consent page (it now shows a Didomi popup, handled by the didomi rule), so it is replaced with ca.yahoo.com and tw.yahoo.com, which still redirect there and pass in GB and DE.

**Rule removals.** Three generated site-specific rules are removed with their specs. auto_CA_f6s.com_yjw and auto_NL_werkenbijdefensie.nl_0cv no longer detect their popups, which the heuristic now rejects. auto_GB_chilternseeds.co.uk_0 matches a hidden element and stalls without opting out; without it the heuristic rejects the popup when it shows. A recheck against the final rule set found every affected site handled, or showing no popup.

**Fixes.** craft-cookie-consent: newer versions of the Craft Cookie Consent plugin show a Reject all button (`#elc-deny-link`), and the settings-based opt-out left the popup open on marcelwanders.com. The rule now clicks Reject all when it is present, with `retry`, because the plugin only binds its click handlers on window load. The settings path stays for older versions. Verified on all spec sites across US, GB, DE, FR, NL, PL, AU, CA and JP, and the rule does not match again after a reload.

143 site runs tested: 2 FIX, 9 STALE SITE, 5 STALE REGION, 5 UNTESTABLE, 122 PASS.

| Rule | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_CA_f6s.com_yjw` | removed, 1 sites removed | The rule no longer detects the f6s.com popup, which the heuristic now rejects; as a site-specific rule it has no other sites. |
| `auto_GB_chilternseeds.co.uk_0` | removed, 1 sites removed | The rule matches a hidden element and stalls without opting out; without it the heuristic rejects the popup when it shows. As a site-specific rule it has no other sites. |
| `auto_NL_werkenbijdefensie.nl_0cv` | removed, 1 sites removed | The rule no longer detects the werkenbijdefensie.nl popup, which the heuristic now rejects; as a site-specific rule it has no other sites. |
| `craft-cookie-consent` | fixed, 1 sites removed | Newer versions of the Craft Cookie Consent plugin show a Reject all button, and the settings-based opt-out left the popup on marcelwanders.com. The rule now clicks Reject all when present, retrying until the plugin binds its handlers on page load. telephonics.com switched to Klaro. |
| `amex` | spec-updated | americanexpress.com no longer shows a consent popup in the US; the spec now skips the US region. |
| `civic-cookie-control` | spec-updated, 2 sites removed | planning.org.uk now uses Google Funding Choices, which the funding-choices rule handles. birmingham.gov.uk answers automated test browsers with 403 Forbidden in most runs; five other sites still cover the rule. |
| `twcc` | spec-updated | wise.com no longer shows a consent popup in the US; the spec now skips the US region. |
| `WP Cookie Notice for GDPR` | spec-updated, 1 sites removed | meyer-koering.de no longer shows a consent popup in any region; three other spec sites still use the CMP. |
| `Yahoo` | spec-updated, 1 sites removed, 2 sites added | www.yahoo.com no longer redirects to the consent.yahoo.com page the rule handles (it now shows a Didomi popup). ca.yahoo.com and tw.yahoo.com still redirect there, and the rule opts out on both in GB and DE. |

## Steps to test this PR:

- `REGION=<GB|DE> npx playwright test tests/yahoo.spec.ts --project=chrome`

title: Rule update: subaru-ca
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220853694937544?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Site-specific pop-up

Adds a `subaru-ca` rule for the cookie notice on Subaru Canada sites (subaru.ca, m.subaru.ca, pr.subaru.ca and the regional subarudealer.ca sites). The notice is a custom banner with only an "I understand" button (no reject option). It sits in the normal page flow rather than being fixed or sticky, so the heuristic popup search does not find it. The rule is scoped to the subaru.ca and subarudealer.ca domains. It detects the `#TermsSelector` banner, treats it as a popup only while it is open (desktop layout, or mobile layout with `.openTermsContainer`), and clicks the acknowledge button. The self-test checks that the banner closed. A spec covering three sites is included.

## Steps to test this PR:

- `npx playwright test tests/subaru-ca.spec.ts --project chrome --workers 2`
- Review the regional screenshots and results linked from the Asana task.

The banner has the checkboxes Notwendige/Präferenzen/Statistiken/Marketing and the buttons "Auswahl erlauben" / "Cookies zulassen". title: Rule update: cookieman
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220839400416704?focus=true

## Description:

Automated autoconsent rule update from CPM triage.

Category: Bug in existing rule

Fixes the cookieman (TYPO3) rule for popup variants it did not handle. When there is no "accept none" button, the rule's opt-out always clicked an `[aria-controls="cookieman-settings"]` settings toggle. That toggle is missing when the settings form is shown inline (autobahn.de, hochschule-bochum.de, smb.museum). It is also missed when its aria-controls lists several ids (b-tu.de). title: Post the Tests / Changed files status to the PR head commit
body:
Many recent PRs never show the `Tests / Changed files` status, even though the Jenkins build runs the tests and calls `githubNotify`.

Jenkins builds a PR by checking out the PR head and merging the target branch into it. The Jenkinsfile assumed that always makes a merge commit and posted the status to `HEAD~1`. When the PR is already up to date with `main` (e.g. opened from the tip of `main` and built before `main` moves), the merge is a no-op, `HEAD` is the PR head, and `HEAD~1` is the `main` commit, so the status lands on `main` instead of the PR. For example, the current tip of `main` carries the statuses of dozens of PR builds, including a failing one.

This posts to `HEAD^1` only when `HEAD` has a second parent, and to `HEAD` otherwise.

title: Rule tests: move spec files to JSON data
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/task/1217862416204870

## Description:

Moves the rule E2E test data from TypeScript specs to plain JSON, so any tool can read which sites and options test a rule without building the project or running Playwright.

- **Data:** every `tests/<name>.spec.ts` becomes `tests/sites/<name>.json`, and every `tests/generated/<name>.spec.ts` becomes `tests/sites/generated/<name>.json`. Each file holds `{ cmp, note?, tests: [{ note?, sites, options? }] }`. The format is in `docs/rule-tests.md`, and the types are in `playwright/spec-types.ts`.
- **Runner:** one generic spec, `tests/rule-sites.spec.ts`, calls the unchanged `generateCMPTests` for each group. `SPECS=onetrust,generated/auto_AU_x` limits a run to some files. Test and describe names stay the same. The only change is that every test now belongs to `rule-sites.spec.ts`.
- **New `timeout` option:** it replaces the `test.describe.configure` call in the banamex spec. It sets a minimum test timeout, so it no longer lowers the longer timeout that Oxylabs runs use.
- **Lint:** `npm run rule-sites-check`, run as part of `npm run lint`, validates the data against a schema generated from the types, so a misspelled option key now fails. It also checks:
  - that each `cmp` names an existing rule
  - that URLs are valid
  - that no group both runs and skips a region
  - that no test is defined twice
- **CI:**
  - `scripts/get-tests-to-run.js` maps a changed rule to data files by rule name rather than by file name. This also covers 14 rules whose spec had a different file name, which never ran in CI before.
  - The Jenkinsfile passes the selection in `SPECS`.
- **Scaffolding:** `npm run create-rule` writes the data file.
  - `scripts/convert-spec-to-json.js` converts spec files from older branches.
  - The labeler globs, AGENTS.md and the skills are updated.
- **Conversion:**
  - Comments became `note` fields.
  - 15 commented-out URLs were dropped (`complianz-categories`, `complianz-optin` ×2, `consentmanager`, `cookiebot`, `cookieinformation`, `datagrail`, `klaro`, `orejime`, `sourcepoint`, `stright`, `tealium` ×2, `wp-cookie-notice` ×2).
  - `tests/flex-orange-pl.spec.ts` is removed, because no rule is named `flex-orange-pl`.

Since this PR touches every data file, Jenkins selects all of them.

## Steps to test this PR:

1. `npm run prepublish`.
2. Compare `REGION=<r> npx playwright test --list --project chrome --reporter=json` on #2981 and on this branch, as multisets of "describe › title". They were identical for NA, US, GB, AU, CA, DE, FR, NL, CH, NO, IT, ES, PL, SE, DK, JP, GW and GM, except for the 2 removed `flex-orange-pl` tests per region. webkit, iphoneSE and firefox list 7,805 tests for DE, the same as chrome.
3. `npm run lint` passes.
4. `SKIP_OPT_IN=1 SPECS=123inkt,banamex,ibkr npx playwright test tests/rule-sites.spec.ts --project chrome` runs those rules' tests. banamex and clientam.co.uk fail without a regional proxy, the same way they do on main.
5. `node scripts/get-tests-to-run.js rules/autoconsent/ionos-de.json lib/cmps/onetrust.ts` prints `ionos` and `onetrust`.
6. `echo zz-test | npm run create-rule` writes `tests/sites/zz-test.json`, and `npm run rule-sites-check` fails until it has sites.

This lets the heuristic recognise simple implied-consent notices such as "We place cookies on your device to keep the site running… Browsing on counts as your consent", which no pattern matched before. title: Remove match_origin_as_fallback and move same-origin iframe rules to the top frame
body:
Task/Issue URL:

## Description:

- Removes `match_origin_as_fallback` from the MV3 and Firefox manifests. See also https://github.com/duckduckgo/duckduckgo-privacy-extension/pull/3822
- Converts same-origin iframe rules to top-frame rules with array selectors:
  - `widiba`: now a top-frame rule that reaches into its same-origin iframe.
  - New generic `cookieform-iframe` rule (top frame, same-origin iframe), replacing the generated modellbau-berlinski.de and huss-licht-ton.de rules.
  - Removes `auto_CH_swisscare.com_arx` (`fullertonhotels.com` handles the site), `auto_CA_nationalarchives.gov.uk_rx0` (popup gone) and `auto_GB_investing.thisismoney.co.uk_0` (clicked a footer link, no longer matches).
  - `bmedonline.es` and `sicredi-frame` stay frame rules: in a frameset, top-frame detection misses late popups.
  - `nojazz`: retries the "customise" click, which is lost if made before the button's handlers attach.
  - `mercadolibre-frame` / `mercadolibre-subdomain`: detect the settings iframe before it hydrates; prehide the settings modal.
- Docs: when to use frame rules.

- `npm run lint && npm run test:lib`

title: Rule sweep: remove 7, fix 1, update specs of 2 rules
body:
Task/Issue URL: https://app.asana.com/1/137249556945/project/1203268166580279/task/1220905832021497?focus=true

## Description:

Automated regression sweep of autoconsent rules, their spec sites and top sites.

**Spec updates.** Several test sites no longer show the popup their spec expects. hotelamourparis.fr moved from macaron to AdOpt, and fairmont-montecarlo.com has an expired TLS certificate. Both leave the macaron spec, replaced by sofitel-munich.com and sofitel-legend-metropole-hanoi.com, which also use the macaron (D-Edge) banner. bloodpressureok.com dropped Complianz for Google Funding Choices, so simon42.com replaces it in the Complianz banner spec. All replacement sites pass in US, GB and DE.

**Rule removals.** Seven generated rules are removed, with their specs. Their sites are handled without them in US, GB and DE, plus the rule's own region:
- The heuristic rejects the popups on everysaving.co.uk, mitarbeiterservice.bayern.de, euro-expos.com, brightondome.org and reading.gov.uk.
- The generic Evidon rule handles lenovo.com.
- bet365.bet.br now only shows a service-unavailable notice, with no consent popup.

**Fix.** The US variant of the AdOpt banner shows a "Do not sell" button, which has no id, where other regions show Reject. The adopt rule now clicks it when there is no Reject button. After a reload, no popup is detected again. The adopt spec swaps instanonimo.com, which no longer uses AdOpt, for hotelamourparis.fr, which shows this variant. The selfTest is off for that site because its AdOpt setup does not store the key the selfTest checks.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

239 site runs tested: 16 STALE SITE, 1 UNTESTABLE, 222 PASS.

| Rule | Change | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_CA_bet365.bet.br_kkx` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The site now only shows a service-unavailable notice, with no consent popup. |
| `auto_DE_lenovo.com_xcv` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The generic Evidon rule handles the popup in every tested region. |
| `auto_DE_mitarbeiterservice.bayern.de_quh` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The heuristic rejects the German popup in every tested region. |
| `auto_FR_euro-expos.com_tok` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The heuristic rejects the French popup in every tested region. |
| `auto_GB_brightondome.org_iz9` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The heuristic rejects the popup in every tested region. |
| `auto_GB_everysaving.co.uk_38t` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The rule no longer acts; the heuristic rejects the popup everywhere. |
| `auto_GB_reading.gov.uk_0` | removed, 1 spec site removed | The heuristic rejects the popup in every tested region. |
| `adopt` | fixed, 1 spec site removed, 1 added | Clicks Do not sell when the US notice has no Reject button. |
| `Complianz banner` | spec-updated, 1 spec site removed, 1 added | bloodpressureok.com dropped Complianz; simon42.com replaces it. |
| `macaron` | spec-updated, 2 spec sites removed, 2 added | Replaces a site now on AdOpt and one with an expired certificate. |
